gateway_client.code_ref: engine route: waav-infer/crates/waav-infer-server/src/lib.rs:1598-1765 (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions); gateway request code to extract: gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:769-814 and :947-1027
gateway_client.notes: Request restrictions enforced by the engine, each answered with HTTP 400 (unsupported_param): a non-empty language or prompt (lib.rs:1564-1574, :1663-1676); any response_format other than json or text, so verbose_json fails (lib.rs:1704-1715); any temperature other than 0 (lib.rs:1576-1596). The model field must be empty or name the loaded family, otherwise model_not_found (lib.rs:1647-1662; engine.rs:2750-2764). Unknown fields such as stream are read and ignored. The response is {"text": ...} only: no timestamps, no confidence, no detected language. Send 16 kHz audio, because the engine otherwise resamples linearly. Limits are the engine defaults (lib.rs:144-166, :48): 100 MiB upload, 64 concurrent requests, a 2 second wait for admission and then HTTP 429 with code admission_rejected, a 30 second deadline per request. A 429 from the engine is load shedding and must not count as a failure for the circuit breaker (gateway/src/core/resilience/infer_reject.rs). Concurrent uploads are folded into one batched forward pass of up to 24 clips with no added delay (waav-infer-server/src/stt_coalescer.rs:26-33, :142-145). The engine binds loopback with no authentication by default and serves one speech-to-text model per process.

transport.disabled_reason: Not implemented. The gateway has no speech-to-text client for the OpenAI Realtime transcription session. Its only code for that socket is a pass-through relay for customers who speak the Realtime protocol themselves, which cannot feed the gateway's own speech-to-text, language-model and text-to-speech chain. Decisions section 12 places the commit transport for OpenAI only.

gateway_client.code_ref: relay only: gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/upstream.rs:113-191 (builds {base}/realtime?intent=transcription for openai and /openai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription with an api-key header for azure_openai); session and event types to reuse: gateway/src/core/realtime/openai/protocol.rs
gateway_client.notes: How the session must work: open the socket with intent=transcription; send session.update with session.type set to transcription, input format audio/pcm at 24 kHz (the gateway must resample from the caller's rate), the transcription model, and turn_detection null; append base64 audio continuously; when the gateway's own voice detector decides the utterance has ended, send input_audio_buffer.commit. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta while the caller speaks and as ...completed after the commit. Completions for different turns may arrive out of order and must be matched by item_id. A commit on an empty buffer is an error. The live models reject the vendor's own voice detection, which is why the gateway owns endpointing here. The intent=transcription query is what the gateway relay, Pipecat and LiveKit dial and what Microsoft's sample uses; it is absent from OpenAI's own pages. The language and context fields are left out of this profile because they differ by model (languages and keywords on gpt-live-transcribe, language and no prompt on gpt-realtime-whisper) and a profile cannot see the model.

gateway_client.notes: Socket ws://host/v1/realtime, read from vLLM source at commit bc21cba. The server sends session.created with an id and no session object. The client must send session.update {model} before anything else; the documentation calls it optional but the code rejects a commit without it (model_not_validated), and a valid update is not acknowledged. Audio is input_audio_buffer.append with base64 PCM16 at 16 kHz mono and nothing else, so the gateway must resample. input_audio_buffer.commit has the opposite meaning to OpenAI's: it starts generation and is sent before the audio; commit with final true ends the audio. A second commit while generation runs is ignored. Text arrives as transcription.delta (append-only) and transcription.done; errors carry a string, not an object. There is no voice detection on the server, so the gateway decides where a turn ends. The route exists only when the loaded model supports the realtime task (Voxtral Realtime and the Qwen3-ASR realtime class); otherwise the upgrade fails with HTTP 403, which looks like a permission error. The Qwen3-ASR class emits text only once per 5 second block, so for conversation it is no better than the file path. vLLM does not reclaim idle streaming sessions, so every open call holds capacity.

gateway_client.notes: Socket ws://host:9000/v1/realtime?intent=transcription; a missing or wrong intent closes the socket with code 1008. The first server frame is conversation.created, not session.created. The client configures with transcription_session.update (input_audio_format pcm16, sample rate 16000 by default, model, BCP-47 language, prompt, endpointing_config, word_boosting), sends input_audio_buffer.append, and may send commit, clear and done. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta and .completed, the latter with words_info, vad_states and is_last_result. Server defaults: sessions expire after 3600 seconds, close after 60 seconds without activity, at most 100 connections, messages up to 10 MB (the page also says 15 MB per append; plan for the smaller). An optional single-use token expires 60 seconds after it is issued. Streaming works only when the container was started with a streaming profile; Whisper, Canary and Parakeet TDT are offline only, Nemotron ASR Streaming and Parakeet CTC or RNNT have streaming profiles. Recorded as endpointing by either side with a silence signal because the session has an endpointing configuration and reports voice states; that reading is an inference and whether the server finalises a segment without a client commit was not confirmed. word_boosting may map to key terms; that mapping is not decided.

gateway_client.notes: A vendor-side segmenting facade: a socket that accepts live audio but runs a batch model once per utterance behind it. Socket /v1/realtime?model=...&intent=transcription&language=...&transcription_model=..., read from speaches source at commit 993994f. The route exists for every model. Incoming audio is treated as 24 kHz and resampled to 16 kHz by the server. The session uses the older OpenAI beta shape (input_audio_transcription.model, turn_detection.type server_vad), not the current session.type transcription shape. Server voice detection defaults: threshold 0.9, no prefix padding, 550 ms of silence. On speech stop or on a client commit the buffer is written to a WAV file and sent to the server's own file transcription; one conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed is published and no delta event. A committed buffer must hold at least 100 ms; a session lasts at most 30 minutes. Authentication is a Bearer header, an X-API-Key header or an api_key query parameter, and no OpenAI-Beta header. response.cancel and conversation.item.truncate are not supported. Whether turn detection can be switched off so that only the gateway commits was not confirmed.

The Deepgram streaming client can already dial another host, but a self-hosted deployment has no route to it: there is no factory arm for this vendor, no trusted channel that carries the deployment's base address to speech-to-text, and the client-settable address override is rejected for in-cluster hosts by the private-address filter.

gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:465-480 (build_websocket_url appends /v1/listen to endpoint_override); override check at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:366-381
gateway_client.notes: For a server that speaks Deepgram's live socket at {base}/v1/listen: a self-hosted Deepgram engine, or WhisperLiveKit, whose /v1/listen is documented as a compatibility subset (interim_results, is_final, speech_final, KeepAlive and CloseStream are supported; Finalize is not). The gateway's Deepgram client never sends Finalize; it closes the stream instead, which fits the subset. WhisperLiveKit fixes raw audio at 16 kHz, while the gateway forwards the caller's bytes unchanged at whatever rate the caller sent (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:634-639) and only declares that rate in the URL (deepgram.rs:498), so audio at any other rate must be resampled first or the transcript is garbage with no error. Behind this socket WhisperLiveKit re-decodes a growing window with Whisper, so latency and GPU cost differ from a natively streaming model. Using this route for streaming Whisper is an idea from the research, not a tested path; no quality signal or context field is assumed.

alibaba-cloud.notes: Canonical id and aliases come from the plugin registry (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1768-1771). The standardized factory that live sessions use accepts only alibaba-cloud and alibaba_cloud (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:400-402). default_model is the client constant DEFAULT_STT_MODEL (gateway/src/core/stt/alibaba_cloud/config.rs:48); its row's only usable transport is today's client, which is recorded as known broken, so a default-configured session keeps that client and the defect is reported in ready.stt. The server has no API-key mapping for this provider (gateway/src/config/mod.rs:679 is the 'Unsupported provider' fall-through), so a session must supply its own key. This file has 50 rows: 41 exact rows keyed by the vendor's wire id, eight pattern rows and the provider default. (1) Model-string rewriting. Before dialing, the client rewrites ten strings (config.rs:164-176). The five that are not vendor ids (qwen3-asr, qwen-asr, paraformer, paraformer-8k, funasr) are model_aliases on the rows of the models the client dials instead. The other five (paraformer-v2, paraformer-8k-v2, paraformer-v1, paraformer-8k-v1, fun-asr) are vendor ids of asynchronous file models; their rows record the streaming model the client substitutes and are refused from Release 3, default on. If the rewrite is removed from the client, those rows need no change. None of the ten is advertised: the plugin metadata lists only qwen3-asr-flash-realtime, paraformer-realtime-v2, paraformer-realtime-8k-v2 and fun-asr-realtime (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:406-411). (2) No model check. Any other string becomes Custom and is sent to the streaming inference socket (config.rs:176, :707-717). (3) Regions. Model availability differs between Singapore, Beijing and US (Virginia), keys are bound to a region, and the client always dials the Beijing legacy host (config.rs:574) unless an endpoint override is set; US (Virginia) has no legacy host. The vendor states that the legacy DashScope domain, the only one the client knows, gets no new features after 2026-09-30. The file transports that the fact-check placed carry region constraints; the streaming rows name their regions in provenance notes only, because a constraint on a row's only usable transport would leave an excluded session without an answer. (4) Retirements. Thirteen ids retire on 2026-10-10 (ten dated snapshots, and the undated fun-asr-mtl, fun-asr-mtl-realtime and sensevoice-v1), including every snapshot behind the default model and behind qwen3-asr-flash. Their rows are 'deprecated' today and carry recheck_on; on that date each must become 'retired' with an empty transports list, and the stable aliases, which carry the same recheck date, must be re-read. (5) Family patterns. The vendor's catalogue lists each model id under exactly one interface: a streaming id sent to the file endpoint is expected to fail, and so is the reverse (inferred from the catalogue; no live call was made). Eight pattern rows therefore sit between the exact rows and the provider default and follow the vendor's naming, as the audit inferred it: an id containing -realtime, -asr-flash-streaming or -asr-flash-message is a streaming socket model; an id containing -filetrans, or a dated fun-asr-202... snapshot, is an asynchronous job with no live path; a dated qwen3-asr-flash-2... or fun-asr-flash-2... snapshot is a synchronous file model. All eight are marked 'assumed'. Each pattern has a different number of literal characters, so precedence between them never depends on file order. The vendor has three model classes: streaming socket models, synchronous short-file models (the ones that need segmentation, served by the regional REST adapter in Release 5, wider vendor coverage and hardening, after a live probe), and asynchronous URL-only jobs (no live path).

amivoice.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1794-1795. The standard factory matches only the exact id 'amivoice' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:403-405), so a session that uses an alias falls to the flat factory. An empty model becomes -a-general (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:48, 560-561). The vendor calls models engines; the model id is the engine id, and it fixes the language. Every one of the 20 vendor engines is served on the WebSocket interface, so none needs a segmented path. The important finding is different: the streaming client does not match the vendor protocol (read on both sides, never probed), and no release builds an AmiVoice file transcriber. Today a session still starts and most likely returns nothing. Following integration decisions section 15, the map keeps that client as the transport of every row whose engine it serves, enabled from Release 0 with status known_broken, and reports the defect instead of refusing the session. Repairing the client (one prefix byte and the audio format names) is far less work than a file-upload adapter. Streaming client, as read: The only test runs against an in-repo mock that answers on any binary frame, so it cannot see the missing prefix (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:660-704). Whether the client fails against the live service was not tested; both sides were read and no key was available. As written, the client forwards each chunk at once as a binary frame, turns vendor U events into interim results about once a second and turns each vendor A event into a result with is_final and is_speech_final both true (client.rs:557-577; messages.rs:210-213). The vendor's speech-start and speech-end events are only logged (client.rs:545-551). The vendor's own detector ends an utterance after 550 ms of silence by default and force-finalises any utterance at 15 seconds. Other defects found by reading: with the header-format names, 16 kHz raw audio works only through a vendor fallback and any other rate is decoded at the wrong rate; the start command, which contains the API key, is written to the debug log (client.rs:155); a start error containing 'auth' is reported as a bad key although the vendor uses the same message for a wrong engine name (client.rs:203-216); a final with empty text is dropped without reading its error code (client.rs:568-577). The vendor disconnects after 600 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout) and after 60 seconds without traffic; a session may last 24 hours. The gateway also accepts short names for engines, for example 'general', 'medical', 'e2e-ja' and 'a2b-multi', and reads every name without regard to case and with underscores as hyphens (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:275-341). The short names whose engine the client sends unchanged are model_aliases of that engine's row (config.rs:275-341). The lookup compares without case but does not turn underscores into hyphens, so the resolver must do that first. Names the client turns into one of its six non-vendor ids (finance, insurance, finance-input, insurance-input, name-input, address-input and their long forms) are not aliases and land on the default row.

assemblyai.notes: Registered under the single id 'assemblyai' (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1691; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:406-408); no aliases. default_model records what happens today for an English or empty language: the gateway picks universal-streaming-english; for any other language it picks universal-streaming-multilingual (gateway/src/core/stt/assemblyai/config.rs:450-456). The field can hold only one id, so the resolver must apply the same language rule before the lookup, also when placeholder_as_unset turns the placeholder 'nova-3' into no model named: the client on its own serves the English model for 'nova-3' whatever the language (config.rs:118-125, 456-459), so the resolver must hand the resolved id to the client. AssemblyAI has three interfaces on three hosts: the streaming socket (streaming.assemblyai.com), the synchronous Sync API (sync.assemblyai.com, which serves universal-3-5-pro only) and the asynchronous job API (api.assemblyai.com). The gateway has one endpoint override shared by all of them and knows only the default and Europe streaming hosts (config.rs:137-153). The streaming client replaces every model id it does not know, including universal-3-6-pro, universal-3-5-pro and universal-2, with universal-streaming-english (config.rs:118-125). The rows for those ids therefore list no streaming transport, and when_unusable records the substitution: such a session keeps today's stream with the warning stt_model_substituted, universal-3-5-pro moves to the Sync API in Release 3, default on, and universal-2 is refused from that release. Fixing the client (send the id, refuse unknown ids) would let those rows list the streaming socket again. The client has a method that sends a forced end-of-turn message (gateway/src/core/stt/assemblyai/client.rs:1084-1106) with no caller; no gateway-driven commit transport is listed because the vendor's current support for that message is not in the fetched evidence. The client's own short name 'multilingual' is a model alias on the universal-streaming-multilingual row.

aws-transcribe.notes: Registered as aws-transcribe with aliases aws_transcribe, amazon-transcribe and transcribe (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:124-130, :1695-1698; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:409-411). Only the spellings aws-transcribe and aws_transcribe reach the standardized factory; amazon-transcribe and transcribe are resolved by the plugin registry and take the flat factory, which drops the standardized features (standard.rs:476), so the resolver must normalise the provider id before lookup. Amazon Transcribe has no base-model parameter; 'standard' and 'medical' are the names gateway/src/config/pricing.rs:275 and :279 already use. 'call-analytics' and 'healthscribe' are labels the vendor audit proposed for two Amazon products the gateway does not implement; no gateway code or price table uses them, and they have rows so that a session naming them is reported as served by standard Amazon Transcribe. Today's client never reads the model id (gateway/src/core/stt/aws_transcribe/config.rs:594; client.rs:488-568). Segmented mode is not available: the only file interface is an asynchronous S3 job, so no file-upload transport is listed. The capability that matters for this provider is language and region: the 18 language codes that are batch-only everywhere are a language constraint on the streaming transports, and the 45 more that cannot be streamed in five regions are not written, because a constraint cannot combine a language with a region. Every final from this client is marked speech-final, so Amazon's own pause detection ends the utterance.

azure_openai.notes: The vendor id for speech-to-text models deployed in Azure OpenAI. It is not Azure AI Speech, which is the separate provider id azure (microsoft-azure). The two spellings are AZURE_OPENAI_NAMES in gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:112, matched by is_azure_openai (:131-134). The id is recognised but has no speech-to-text plugin (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs registers it for text-to-speech at :1826 and as a realtime alias at :2007-2008 only); a live call that names such a deployment is refused today with the codes unsupported_deployment and stt_not_streaming (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and :815-826), which integration decisions addendum A1 keeps for an Azure OpenAI deployment the segmented engine does not cover, until the Bud-side check on them is answered. The upload route forwards the file whole (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:839-913). On Azure the model string on the wire is the name the customer gave the deployment, and it goes into the URL path (self_hosted.rs:171-200). budapp publishes the credential's deployment id in voice_table.model when there is one and the model name otherwise (transcribe.rs:827-829). Today's leg code sends config.stt.model when set, otherwise voice_table.model (bud_legs.rs:216-226). Because a deployment name says nothing about the base model, a row is found from the base model the deployment override declares (underlying_model), else from the name itself, which matches an exact or pattern row only when the customer named the deployment after the base model, else the provider default row, which is file upload. The name sent to Azure is always the deployment name. default_model is null because there is no deployment to fall back to; an empty model is a configuration error (self_hosted.rs:177-183).

prerequisites.detail: The pro API needs the token scope brain_enhanced_asr.

baidu.notes: Registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1774-1775; dispatched at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:413. MODEL KEY: the model id is Baidu's dev_pid, an integer on the wire, written here as a string. Language is fixed by the dev_pid. An empty model resolves to 1537 (gateway/src/core/stt/baidu/config.rs:39, fallback at :118). EVIDENCE QUALITY: Baidu's documentation hosts could not be reached by the audit or the fact-check. First-hand evidence is Baidu's official GitHub demo code; everything else is a third-party mirror of the official pages or a search excerpt that cites them, and nothing could be tested live. Rows that rest only on second-hand evidence are marked assumed. STREAMING CLIENT (adapter native, known_broken; read from code and official demo code, never run against the vendor; all paths under gateway/src/core/stt/baidu/): (1) The START frame is built from the API Key as 'appid' and the Secret Key as 'appkey' (client.rs:512-519), and appid is a string (messages.rs:27); Baidu's demos send an integer AppID and the API Key. The api_key|secret_key credential (config.rs:470-486) has no place for an AppID, so authentication very probably fails. (2) err_no is a required field of the response (messages.rs:138), so HEARTBEAT frames probably fail to parse. (3) Unknown model ids become 1537 (config.rs:118) and STTConfig.language is never read. (4) Confidence is hard-coded to 1.0 (client.rs:663). The repository mock ignores the START frame (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:803-827), so its passing test does not cover the credential mismatch. FILE UPLOAD (adapter regional_rest, not implemented): recognize_short_audio (client.rs:694-767) has no caller, targets https://vop.baidu.com/server_api only (config.rs:404-410), uses a 30 second HTTP timeout (client.rs:80) and returns an error for an empty result or any non-zero err_no (client.rs:756-766). The client's REST mode buffers without limit and never flushes (client.rs:880-883). The OAuth token cache is per client instance; a process-wide cache is needed. The gateway's Baidu error-code table (messages.rs:325) disagrees with the vendor's and must not be reused. From search excerpts of the official error table (not read first-hand): 3300 input parameter incorrect (never retry); 3301 audio quality too poor (a normal no-speech outcome, drop the segment); 3302 authentication failed (refresh the token once); 3303 back-end busy and 3307 back-end recognition error (retry once; the gateway labels 3303 'Audio file too long', messages.rs:341-342); 3304 concurrency exceeded, counted per AppID (back off and retry); 3305 daily quota exceeded; 3308 audio longer than 60 seconds and 3309 audio data problem (never retry). Concurrency is counted per AppID across all callers, so the limiter must be shared by every session on the credential. The adapter picks the endpoint from the row's dialect.wire: baidu_server_api or baidu_pro_api. The file API needs exactly the api_key|secret_key credential the gateway already accepts, so it is the first Baidu transport that can work. STATE TODAY: the streaming client is the native transport, enabled from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, and reported as known broken in ready.stt rather than refused (integration decisions, section 15); each native transport carries its defect. The file transport (regional_rest) is enabled from Release 5, wider vendor coverage and hardening, and only after a live probe with a real key (decisions section 12). Until then a model the gateway has no working path for is refused or warned as its when_unusable says. Segmentation is required for 80001 on first-hand evidence; 1637 and 1837 need it only if the socket rejects them, which is unverified. 8001 (a self-trained model, chosen with lm_id) is rowed as file upload only because nothing shows it on the socket. The two far-field ids, 1936 (file API) and 19362 (real-time), are rowed as retired. config/pricing.rs has no Baidu entries, so rows carry no pricing_key.

prerequisites.detail: The service id and the compute address come from the vendor's pipeline configuration call.

bhashini.notes: Registered in the plugin registry as bhashini with seven aliases (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1758-1761); the standard factory matches only the exact string bhashini (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:414-416). This is the Government of India service at bhashini.gov.in; the company at bhashini.ai is unrelated. The vendor exposes service ids, each bound to one model and reached through a pipeline id. The gateway's model field only selects a pipeline: 'ai4bharat' or 'a4b' selects the AI4Bharat pipeline and anything else the MeitY pipeline (gateway/src/core/stt/bhashini/config.rs:561-564). The service id then comes from the vendor's configuration call at run time (client.rs:296-301), so a customer cannot name one today and an empty model cannot be resolved to a row in advance; default_model is therefore null and such sessions use the provider default row. The existing client buffers the audio and uploads it once, when it is disconnected (client.rs:506-552). That happens at hang-up, or earlier when the caller's application sends the end-of-audio message, which makes the gateway disconnect and reconnect the speech-to-text client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:301-314, gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672). So a conversation gets no transcript while it is in progress, and audio beyond 10 MB is rejected (client.rs:51). A push-to-talk application that sends the end-of-audio message after each utterance is therefore the one use that can get a transcript today, provided the vendor's reply parses (see the next sentences). Even the transcript at hang-up is doubtful: a call longer than about 30 s is uploaded as one clip beyond the length the vendor documents without its voice-activity pre-processor, and a response in the vendor's documented shape (audio set to null) would fail to parse and be retried twice more (messages.rs:354-359, client.rs:356-400). That is inferred from reading and was not run. The vendor also documents a Socket.IO live interface that takes a service id; the gateway has no client for it and the audit recommends against building one now. Eight of the twelve service ids begin with 'bhashini/' and four with the alias 'ai4bharat/', so the rows are keyed by the full wire string and no provider prefix is stripped. The only live contact with the vendor during the research was unauthenticated: the compute endpoint answered HTTP 403 'Not authenticated' and the Socket.IO endpoint answered with a handshake, which confirms that both exist. Nothing was transcribed, which is why every row says it was verified from documentation.

cartesia.notes: Registered under the single id 'cartesia' (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1683; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:417-419); no aliases. An empty model resolves to ink-whisper (gateway/src/core/stt/cartesia/config.rs:145, 355-358). Today's client also reads the literal id 'nova-3' as no model chosen (config.rs:352-358), which placeholder_as_unset reproduces in the resolver; the Python client library and the dashboard send 'nova-3' for every provider when the caller chose no model (clients_sdk/python/bud_waav/ws/session.py:942; clients_sdk/dashboard/js/websocket.js:107). Every Cartesia model accepts a live stream on the manual socket, so no model needs the call cut into uploaded utterances; the synchronous file endpoint serves the ink-whisper family only and is a fallback no release builds. The change that matters for this vendor is a third way of working, between vendor-ended streaming and file upload: keep the socket and let the gateway's own voice detector send Cartesia's finalize command. The vendor designed the manual socket for that and calls it crucial for low latency; the gateway never sends it. That transport is enabled from Release 4, live-only models and low latency, and is listed first on every row. Two code paths build the client. Live sessions use the standardized path, which forwards the configured model (config.rs:346-358; gateway/src/handlers/ws/config_handler.rs:1921, 1947). The older flat path ignores the model and always uses ink-whisper (config.rs:320-329), and a configuration update goes through that flat path, so it resets the model to ink-whisper (gateway/src/core/stt/cartesia/client.rs:783-795). The streaming client has only been run against mocks and differs from Cartesia's current documentation in its authentication parameter, pinned API version and command format; a live probe is the first thing to do for this provider.

deepgram.notes: Registered under the single id 'deepgram' (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1666; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:397-399); no aliases. default_model records what happens today: the gateway omits an empty model from the request (gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:486-491) and Deepgram documents base-general, a legacy model, as its default; this is inferred and was not observed on a live call. The plan should make the gateway send an explicit current model and change this field in the same commit. Until then the resolver must use default_model only to find the row for a session that named no model, and the client must keep omitting the model: base-general is not in the streaming specification's closed model list, so sending it explicitly could be rejected. Deepgram has three kinds of model. Nova, Enhanced and Base ids stream on wss /v1/listen, which the gateway already does, and also have a synchronous file endpoint. The six Whisper Cloud ids are file-only and need the call cut into uploaded utterances. The two Flux ids stream only on wss /v2/listen, for which the gateway has no client, and have no file endpoint. The gateway checks no model id today, so Whisper Cloud and Flux ids are accepted at session setup and fail at the vendor. Not given exact rows: the specification value 'custom', and nova-3-pharma, nova-2-phonecall and nova-2-atc, which appear in documentation tables but in neither specification list; they resolve through the family rows or the provider default. Deepgram's rate limits are concurrency limits per project, not per API key, so two keys in one project share them and the gateway cannot see the project from the key. The gateway keeps one circuit breaker per provider name (gateway/src/core/resilience/registry.rs:73-77) and counts a rate-limit response as a failure (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:136-141), so file uploads for Whisper Cloud need a breaker key of their own or they could cut off Nova streaming sessions. The hosts restriction of Whisper Cloud is recorded as constraints.regions on its file transports.

elevenlabs.notes: Registered as `elevenlabs` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1674); live sessions build the socket client through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:420-422). The vendor has two disjoint model families: scribe_v2_realtime on a WebSocket, and scribe_v2 and scribe_v2_medical on a synchronous file endpoint. The gateway keeps one closed list of realtime ids (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/config.rs:189) and treats every other id as a file model (elevenlabs/batch.rs:63-65), which is why the provider default row is file upload. A live session that names a file model fails at setup today (config.rs:391), pinned by the test a_live_session_never_gets_the_batch_client (standard.rs:950). An empty model on a live session stays on the socket, because the configuration keeps its scribe_v2_realtime default (config.rs:331, :554-568) and the check at :391 skips an empty id; default_model records that. On the upload route an empty model resolves to scribe_v2 instead (elevenlabs/batch.rs:47), so the default depends on the route. The flat constructor ignores the configured model and always uses scribe_v2_realtime (client.rs:823-826). The spelling eleven_labs is accepted as a vendor name by the language mapper (gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:217) and by text-to-speech handlers (gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1337), but not by the speech-to-text dispatcher (standard.rs:420) or the plugin registry (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1674), so it is not listed as an alias; a live session that names it does not reach this client (inferred from the dispatch arms, not run).

fpt-ai.notes: Legacy FPT.AI Speech on api.fpt.ai. 'general' is the engine segment of the vendor URL path (/hmi/asr/general); it resolves an empty model to the documented row instead of the provider default. Registry id and aliases: gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1799-1800; the standardized factory that live sessions use accepts fpt-ai, fpt_ai, fptai and fpt (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:423-425). The gateway's only client is a request-and-response HTTP client that buffers the whole call and uploads at hang-up, at a client commit (audio_end disconnects the client, which flushes: gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672, gateway/src/core/stt/fpt_ai/client.rs:345-349) or after 9.6 MB; it is not a transport. The server has no API-key mapping for this provider (gateway/src/config/mod.rs:679). FPT AI Marketplace (mkp-api.fptcloud.com, OpenAI-compatible) is a separate host this client does not reach; it listed no speech-to-text model on 2026-10-03 and has no row here. If a model is relisted there, serve it as an OpenAI-compatible deployment.

gladia.notes: Aliases are the three registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1724-1725 plus 'gladia-stt' from the static table at gateway/src/plugin/dispatch.rs:296. The standardized factory matches only the exact id 'gladia' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:426), so the resolver must map an alias to 'gladia' first. native_model_handling is 'ignored' because today's client never reads the configured model and always sends solaria-1 (gateway/src/core/stt/gladia/config.rs:493, 541-551). Gladia has two models with documentation. solaria-1 streams on the live socket, which the gateway already uses. solaria-3 is accepted only by the pre-recorded API, an asynchronous job (upload, create, poll); Gladia has no synchronous file endpoint that can select a model (its older synchronous route has no model field). A third id, solaria-fusion, appears only in the pre-recorded specification's model list and is left to the provider default. Gladia's public model listing endpoint returns solaria-1 only and cannot feed this map. The pre-recorded API must never be sent the same audio twice, because each accepted job is billed. The Python client library and the dashboard send the model 'nova-3' for every provider when the caller chose none (clients_sdk/python/bud_waav/ws/session.py:942; clients_sdk/dashboard/js/websocket.js:107); placeholder_as_unset makes the resolver read it as no model named, so those sessions resolve to solaria-1.

prerequisites.detail: The legacy gRPC service needs the vendor's CA certificate, which today's client reads only from the process environment (GNANI_CERTIFICATE_PATH or GNANI_CERTIFICATE_CONTENT).

gnani.notes: Registered in the plugin registry as gnani with the aliases gnani-ai, gnani.ai and vachana (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1708-1711). The standard factory matches only the exact string gnani (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:427), and gnani is missing from get_supported_stt_providers (gateway/src/core/stt/mod.rs:549-581). The vendor sells one current model, Gnani Prisma v2.5, on its Vachana platform (api.vachana.ai): a synchronous file endpoint, a realtime WebSocket that cuts utterances itself and returns final text only, and an asynchronous batch API. The gateway speaks to none of them. Its only Gnani client is gRPC to the older asr.gnani.ai service, with different credentials, and that client never validates or sends the model, so today every model string is routed to the legacy service. default_model is set to the vendor's only current model as a planning choice: today's code has no default beyond the placeholder string 'default' (gateway/src/core/stt/gnani/config.rs:100), which has its own row describing the legacy service. The Vachana endpoints need a Vachana API key sent as X-API-Key-ID; the gateway's server configuration only knows the legacy token (gateway/src/config/mod.rs:672-677). The vendor's own Pipecat and LiveKit integrations upload one utterance per request to the same file endpoint, so the segmented pattern is the vendor's documented usage. The only live contact with the vendor during the research was one unauthenticated request to the file endpoint, which returned HTTP 401; that confirms the endpoint exists and shows one of its two error shapes. Nothing was transcribed, which is why every row says it was verified from documentation.

google.notes: Registered as google with no aliases (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:74-84, :1669-1671; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:428). The client speaks only the gRPC StreamingRecognize method of Speech-to-Text V2 (gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:185) and copies the model string to the request unchanged (gateway/src/core/stt/google/streaming.rs:249); it has no model, region or language check. default_model is latest_long because that is the default the client declares (gateway/src/core/stt/google/config.rs:122). It is a lookup key only. The constructor paths pass an empty model to Google as an empty string (gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:464-477; gateway/src/core/stt/base.rs:592), so a session with no model does not send latest_long today, and what Google does with an empty model on the implicit recognizer is unverified (the audit inferred that Google rejects it). If the resolver writes this default into the request it changes the wire for those sessions and needs its own test. The client dials the recognizer location global unless the session supplies provider_extras.location on the standardized path (gateway/src/core/stt/google/config.rs:7, :126, :175-177); the flat constructor path cannot set a location. Model availability depends on the recognizer location (global, us, eu or a region) and, for chirp_2, on the language. The chirp_2 language limit is a constraint on its streaming transport; locations are not written as constraints, because Google's sources disagree and a wrong constraint would refuse sessions that work (Google names its Locations API as the live source). Every final from this client is marked speech-final, so Google's own finalization ends the utterance on the streaming path. The client has no handling for a model that ends the stream after every utterance (latest_short, and probably short): each close is treated as a dropped stream and uses up the reconnect budget, which is why the latest_short streaming client is marked known broken. Not listed as a transport: BatchRecognize, an asynchronous job that reads only from Cloud Storage.

groq.notes: Registered as `groq` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1705); live sessions build it through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:429). Groq has no streaming speech-to-text interface: both models are served by one synchronous multipart endpoint that is wire-compatible with OpenAI's. The existing client buffers audio and uploads only at hang-up, when the buffer reaches 20 MB, or when the client ends its audio by hand (an audio_end message on /ws, or a buffer commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), because the default flush strategy is OnDisconnect and no configuration path sets another (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/config.rs:521; client.rs:873-902), so a normal live call produces no transcript while it is in progress. Either act makes the voice manager disconnect and reconnect the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:301-322, also called from gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:1353-1354; gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672), and the disconnect uploads the buffer (client.rs:1085-1108). A push-to-talk client that ends each utterance itself is therefore the one kind of session that gets usable text from this provider during a call today. The same disconnect clears the result callback (client.rs:1114-1115) and nothing registers it again, so a second such act in the same session probably delivers nothing (inferred from reading, not run). An empty model resolves to whisper-large-v3-turbo (config.rs:47, :540-543). The client reads underscores as hyphens before it matches its short aliases (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/config.rs:126), so large_v3 also selects whisper-large-v3; the rows list only the hyphen spellings as model_aliases. There is no model allow-list: unknown ids are sent verbatim, and plugin metadata still advertises the retired distil-whisper-large-v3-en (mod.rs:146).

huawei-cloud.notes: Registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1784; dispatched at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:430-432. MODEL KEY: the model id is Huawei's 'property' string, which encodes language, sample rate and domain; there is no separate model or language parameter. An empty model resolves to chinese_16k_general (gateway/src/core/stt/huawei_cloud/config.rs:40, fallback at :230). The gateway accepts a region suffix on the model, for example chinese_16k_general@cn-north-4 (config.rs:777-783; key_normalisation), and an unrecognised region silently becomes cn-north-4 (config.rs:779). REGIONS: region limits of the short-audio interface are region constraints on the file transports; those of the real-time socket stay in each row's provenance notes. Documented SIS hosts are sis-ext.cn-north-4, sis-ext.cn-east-3, sis-ext.ap-southeast-3 and sis-ext.me-east-1. The gateway's region list (config.rs:75-91) has ap-southeast-1 and ap-southeast-2, which the vendor does not list for SIS, and lacks me-east-1. STREAMING CLIENT (adapter native, known_broken; read from code, vendor documentation and DNS, never run against the vendor; all paths under gateway/src/core/stt/huawei_cloud/): (1) China regions dial sis.{region}.myhuaweicloud.com (config.rs:25, :128-134); that host is absent from DNS for cn-north-4 and cn-east-3, so the socket cannot connect there, and the Bangkok region in the gateway's list has no SIS host at all. (2) The parser expects resp_type STARTED and ENDED, a top-level 'result' and an integer error_code (messages.rs:219-260); the vendor sends START, EVENT, RESULT with segments[].result, and string codes such as SIS.0002, so a real result yields no transcript and a real error fails to parse. (3) Only the one-sentence mode /rasr/short-stream is reachable (config.rs:387-388; nothing sets the mode); it has a one-minute limit and no vendor end-of-speech detection, and END is sent only at shutdown (client.rs:158-163). A call needs /rasr/continue-stream (5 hours, vendor end-of-speech detection). (4) Unknown model ids become chinese_16k_general (config.rs:230), and STTConfig.language and sample_rate are never read (config.rs:762-798). (5) Model aliases written with a hyphen can never match: from_str replaces '-' with '_' before it compares (config.rs:213), but the arms still spell zh-cn, zh-yue, zh-sichuan and zh-minnan (config.rs:214-224), so 'zh-yue' becomes Mandarin. The repository mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1628, :1652) uses the same undocumented schema, so its passing test covers none of this. PER-UTTERANCE SOCKET (adapter planned_commit, which no release builds; inferred from the documentation): the one-sentence mode ignores vad_head, vad_tail and max_seconds and returns the final result shortly after the client's END, which makes it a per-utterance primitive the gateway's own detector can drive. Whether one WebSocket may carry several START and END cycles is unverified, so plan for a connection per utterance. An idle socket is closed with SIS.0304. FILE UPLOAD (adapter regional_rest, not implemented): recognize_short_audio (client.rs:705-770) builds the documented JSON request but has no caller, returns text only (dropping score and word_info, client.rs:766-769), and belongs to a client mode that buffers without limit and never flushes (client.rs:891-894). Its URL comes from get_short_asr_url (config.rs:680-687), which shares the dead China host. MAX_SHORT_AUDIO_DURATION_SECS is 30 (config.rs:52) while the vendor limit is one minute. Each client instance logs in with a password; a process-wide token cache is needed. Treat SIS.0312 (concurrency exceeded) as back-pressure. The '4 MB' limit is recorded with the decimal reading, the lower one. STATE TODAY: the streaming client is the native transport, enabled from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, and reported as known broken in ready.stt rather than refused (integration decisions, section 15); each native transport carries its defect. The file transport (regional_rest) is enabled from Release 5, wider vendor coverage and hardening, and only after a live probe with a real key (decisions section 12). Until then a model the gateway has no working path for is refused or warned as its when_unusable says. Segmentation is required for chinese_16k_travel, english_16k_common and english_8k_common; the last is a model the vendor no longer maintains and is marked legacy. The gateway's speech-to-text feature table has no huawei-cloud row, and config/pricing.rs has no Huawei entries, so rows carry no pricing_key.

ibm-watson.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1700-1701 and matched by the standard factory at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:433-435. default_model is only part of the truth: with an empty model the gateway picks a _Multimedia id from the session language (gateway/src/core/stt/ibm_watson/config.rs:600-618) and falls back to en-US_Multimedia; four of those language defaults (es-LA, zh-CN, ar-MS and hi-IN _Multimedia) are not IBM models. Every IBM model (18 large speech ids, 21 telephony ids including the beta medical one, 12 multimedia ids) is served on the WebSocket interface and on synchronous HTTP, so no IBM model needs a segmented path; file upload is a fallback, and a gateway-driven stop on the open socket is the better way to give the gateway the turn boundary. Rows are an allow-list: today any string is sent to IBM unchanged. Streaming client, as read: Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). The keep-alive is 64 bytes of silence after 10 seconds without audio (client.rs:246-263), which does not meet IBM's rule of 15 seconds of audio in any 30 second window. IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

iflytek.notes: Registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1763-1766; dispatched at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:436-437 (which also accepts 'ifly'). MODEL KEY: iFlytek has no model parameter. Rows are keyed by the vendor's business.domain value, which matches how the gateway picks the socket today: a model string containing 'realtime', 'stream' or 'ist' selects the real-time socket and anything else, including an empty string, selects the short-form socket with domain 'iat' (gateway/src/core/stt/iflytek/config.rs:422-436). default_model is therefore 'iat' although the vendor has no model field. Three glob rows, '*realtime*', '*stream*' and '*ist*', mirror that substring routing so that a string the gateway sends to the real-time socket is not described as the short-form product; they are marked assumed and should be deleted when model routing becomes an exact lookup. The client targets the international (Singapore) hosts only. NO FILE UPLOAD: segmentation by file upload is neither needed nor possible. Every product that can serve a call is a WebSocket stream, and the only file API is an asynchronous job with a stated floor of about 20 seconds. STREAMING CLIENT (adapter native, known_broken; read from code and vendor documentation, never run against the vendor; paths under gateway/src/core/stt/iflytek/ unless stated): (1) A short-form session holds one utterance: the vendor's final result sets session_ended (client.rs:253-257), the next tick returns Completed (client.rs:191-195) and the supervisor exits without redialling (gateway/src/core/websocket/reconnectable_stream.rs:374-376). Every later send_audio fails (client.rs:841-844) while is_ready stays true (client.rs:827-829). The repository test states this is by design (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:578-580). (2) Results are slices the client is expected to join and, for 'rpl' slices, replace; the client emits each slice alone (messages.rs:481-486, client.rs:489-508), so a final carries only the last fragment, and an empty last slice emits no final at all. (3) Confidence is the average of a field the vendor documents as reserved, or an invented 0.95 (messages.rs:489-500). (4) On the short-form socket the end of an utterance is the vendor's silence timeout vad_eos, 2000 ms by default (config.rs:439), so end of speech to final is at least two seconds. (5) On the real-time socket the client always sends domain 'iat' (config.rs:436) and vad_eos, where the vendor documents the domains ist_open, ist, ist_hy, ist_huanyu and sp_ist_vais, the parameter 'punc', 16 kHz audio only and no vad_eos; and it marks a result final only when data.status is 2, which on that socket follows the client's own end marker, so probably no final arrives before hang-up (inferred). (6) An unknown language falls back to Mandarin (config.rs:416), and Cantonese is sent as language 'zh_hk' with accent 'cantonese' (config.rs:126, :174), which is not a vendor value: the vendor selects Cantonese with language 'zh_cn' plus accent 'cantonese' on both sockets. (7) vad_eos is copied from the customer's endpointing_ms without a bound (config.rs:469-471; validate() at config.rs:496-525 never checks it), although the vendor's maximum is 10000 ms. (8) Once the first frame has gone, the loop sends a frame every 40 ms even when it has no audio (client.rs:198), so zero-length frames flow during silence, the vendor's 10 second idle timer never fires, and silence is never withheld. (9) After the first utterance the session is not closed or redialled: each audio frame the caller sends produces one error message to the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:130-133; LiveKit path gateway/src/handlers/ws/config_handler.rs:2947-2954). PER-UTTERANCE SOCKET (adapter planned_commit, which no release builds): open a short-form session when the gateway's detector reports speech (pre-roll first), stream in real time, send the end marker {"data":{"status":2}} when the detector reports end of speech, then open the next session; rotate before 60 seconds. Set vad_eos to its maximum of 10000 ms so the vendor's silence timeout does not end the session first. The vendor asks for 1280 bytes every 40 ms and warns that a shorter interval may cause incorrect recognition. Results must be assembled by slice number with replacements applied. This adapter shares its speech start and stop events with the segmented engine. STATE TODAY: the streaming client is the native transport, enabled from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, and reported as known broken in ready.stt rather than refused (integration decisions, section 15); each native transport carries its defect. No release builds a file or commit transport for iFlytek (decisions section 12: its only file interface is a slow asynchronous job). Speed Transcription task types, which today's client silently streams as domain 'iat', are refused from Release 3, default on. config/pricing.rs has no iFlytek entries, so rows carry no pricing_key.

microsoft-azure.notes: The plugin registry's canonical id is microsoft-azure with alias azure (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:92-98, :1677-1680); the live speech-to-text name tables accept only those two spellings (gateway/src/plugin/dispatch.rs:257 and :280; gateway/src/core/stt/mod.rs:400). microsoft_azure is accepted only by a vendor-name helper on the REST audio routes (gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1503-1505); a live session using that spelling would be refused today as an unknown provider (gateway/src/plugin/registry.rs:310-320; inferred from reading, not run), so it is listed as an alias for the resolver to normalise, not because it works today. The standardized factory matches only the spelling 'azure' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:412), so a session naming microsoft-azure falls to the flat factory (:476) and loses region, api_base and every standardized feature; the resolver must normalise the provider id before lookup. The reach of that split is narrower than it looks: a Bud voice-agent leg copies the deployment's vendor string into the session (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:223), and Bud publishes Azure Speech under the vendor name azure (comment at gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:108-109), so Bud legs reach the standardized factory and only sessions that name microsoft-azure take the flat one. Azure Speech real-time recognition has no model id on the wire, so the model string is a name the gateway defines, and today's client never reads it (gateway/src/core/stt/azure/config.rs:552, :670), so the capability lookup must run before the client is built. Sessions are expected to reach this provider with model ids other than 'default' (inferred from two things read in the repository): the gateway's own documentation tells customers to put a Custom Speech endpoint id in the model field (gateway/docs/azure-stt.md:76, :183-191), and a Bud deployment's stored model string is copied into the session (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:223-226; a comment at gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:108 says Bud publishes Azure Speech models under names of the form azure/speech/..., the exact speech-to-text strings were not confirmed). Every such id resolves to the provider default row, so that row decides the path of those sessions. 'llm-speech' is a proposed gateway sentinel for the LLM Speech product, which has no vendor model string. Not listed as transports: batch transcription and Whisper inside Azure Speech (asynchronous jobs that can take up to 30 minutes to start) and the 60-second short-audio REST call (Microsoft positions it as a last resort). Azure OpenAI audio models (whisper, gpt-transcribe, the gpt-4o transcribe family, gpt-live-transcribe, gpt-realtime-whisper) belong to the separate provider id azure_openai (rows/azure_openai.json), not to this file.

naver-clova.notes: NAVER Cloud Platform CLOVA speech recognition. The vendor has no model parameter; its four speech-to-text products are chosen by endpoint and credential type, so the row keys are gateway-defined product aliases (csr, clova-speech-short, clova-speech-long, clova-speech-streaming) and an empty model resolves to csr. Only CSR is implemented, and today's client never reads the session's model, so every NAVER session reaches CSR (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/config.rs:276-334). The client registered today (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/client.rs) buffers the whole call and uploads after 60 s of audio, at hang-up, or when the client sends audio_end (which disconnects and reconnects the speech-to-text client, gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672). It is not a transport: when_unusable on each row records what a live session gets from it. It also fails badly: after one failed upload it never clears its buffer, so every later audio frame is refused with an error and copies the 1.9 MB buffer again, even while the breaker is open (client.rs:117-120, :152 and :354-360; gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:130-133). Only the 'csr' row and the default row describe an endpoint that today's credentials can reach: the key must have the form client_id|client_secret (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/config.rs:283-298). The three CLOVA Speech rows need a different credential (a per-domain secret, and for long-sentence recognition a per-domain address) that this configuration cannot carry. Three of the four products are file-only at the vendor and their file endpoints answer in one request, so segmentation is both required and feasible; only CSR is placed in a release (decisions section 12). The vendor's minimum sample rate is 16 kHz. Aliases: the registry accepts naver_clova, naverclova, naver, clova, csr and two Korean spellings (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1788-1791); the standardized factory omits one Korean spelling (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:439).

availability.note: Free for study; no commercial use; uploaded audio may be reused for research.

nectec.notes: AI for Thai (Partii) speech-to-text. Registry id and aliases: gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1809-1810; the standardized factory that live sessions use accepts nectec, aiforthai, ai4thai, partii, partii5 and partii4 (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:444-446). The provider aliases partii4 and partii5 select the provider, not the engine. The vendor has no model parameter; partii4 and partii5 are gateway-defined ids mapped to URL paths, and the client's other spellings of them (config.rs:108-117) are model_aliases on their rows. default_model is partii4, which is NOT what the code does today. Today an empty or unknown model becomes partii5 (gateway/src/core/stt/nectec/config.rs:84-85, :234-238), whose vendor endpoint returns 404, so a default-configured session cannot transcribe. The fact-check requires that partii5 stop being the default, and partii4 is the only engine whose endpoint answers, so the map resolves an empty model to it and the client default must be changed in the same step: until it is, a push-to-talk session that names no model resolves to the partii4 row and keeps today's client, which dials partii5 and fails. The gateway's only client is an HTTP client that uploads after every 30 s of received audio, at hang-up or at a client commit (client.rs:510-545); it is not a transport. The vendor's public catalogue lists Partii as inactive. Thai only.

openai.notes: Registered as `openai` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1687); live sessions build it through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:447). The existing client is HTTP request and response only. On a live call it buffers audio and uploads only at hang-up, when the buffer reaches 20 MB, or when the client ends its audio by hand (an audio_end message on /ws, or a buffer commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), because the default flush strategy is OnDisconnect and no configuration path sets another (gateway/src/core/stt/openai/config.rs:651; client.rs:793-823), so a normal call gets no transcript while it is in progress. Either act makes the voice manager disconnect and reconnect the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:301-322, also called from gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:1353-1354; gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672), and the disconnect uploads the buffer (client.rs:886-897). A push-to-talk client that ends each utterance itself is therefore the one kind of session that gets usable text from this provider during a call today. The same disconnect clears the result callback (client.rs:902-903) and nothing registers it again, so a second such act in the same session probably delivers nothing (inferred from reading, not run). There is no streaming speech-to-text client for OpenAI, so no native transport appears in any row. default_model is gpt-transcribe by integration decision (section 15, awaiting sign-off), while today's code still resolves an empty model to whisper-1 (config.rs:63-67, :671-674), which the vendor removes on 2027-02-26; the code default has to move to gpt-transcribe with it. There is no model allow-list: unknown ids are sent verbatim (config.rs:671-693). OpenAI, self-hosted servers, Azure OpenAI, Groq and WaaV Infer speak the same multipart request: the adapters openai_transcriptions, azure_openai_transcriptions and groq_transcriptions are one implementation with different hosts, authentication and limits. For any id outside its three-entry model list the client labels the vendor call span with a family fallback instead of the id sent (client.rs:438-444; config.rs:109-115), which matters for per-model metering. The language a session configures is mapped to ISO 639-1, with `auto` omitted, before the client is built on the /ws path (gateway/src/handlers/ws/config.rs:475-504; gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:218-222); the segmented adapter must take that mapped value, while the DAG node passes its own default en-US unmapped (gateway/src/dag/nodes/provider.rs:334-343). Unlike self-hosted and Azure OpenAI deployments, which are refused before a client is built (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and, for voice-agent legs, :815-826), an `openai` session is not refused today; both sites are where an interim refusal of OpenAI file models would go.

prerequisites.detail: An on-premises server needs a trusted way to configure a private address.

phonexia.notes: Registered in the plugin registry as phonexia with the aliases phonexia-stt and phonexia_stt (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1733-1736). Phonexia is on-premises software: there is no vendor-hosted endpoint, no documented authentication, and every limit is a deployment setting. The current product, Speech Platform 4 (release 2026.07.0), has two engines, and both transcribe complete files only. The gateway's existing client is a WebSocket streaming client that matches no Phonexia product and refuses to connect unless WAAV_PHONEXIA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED is set (gateway/src/core/stt/phonexia/client.rs:276-290), so no Phonexia call works today. The gateway reads the model field as a result type (config.rs:425-430) and the api_key field as the server address (config.rs:407-410). default_model is null because the evidence does not establish which engine an empty model should select; an empty or unknown model falls to the provider default row. The server address is checked against private networks (config.rs:282-287), which blocks the usual on-premises address. On gRPC one endpoint serves one language (6th generation) or one model (Whisper), so a deployment needs one configured endpoint for each.

revai.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1729-1730 and matched by the standard factory at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:451-453. An empty model resolves to the default transcriber, for which the gateway omits the transcriber query parameter (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:146-151 and 541-553); the vendor treats that as 'machine'. Rev AI needs no segmented path: its live-capable models stream and the gateway already streams to them. Its other transcribers exist only on an asynchronous job API answered in minutes, so they get rows with no transport and a refusal reason, never a file-upload transport. Rev AI has a European deployment (wss://ec1.api.rev.ai/speechtotext/v1/stream/) that the gateway cannot select except through an endpoint override. No transport on this vendor is verified live; the gateway holds no Rev AI key. The gateway's model gate compares the model string exactly, after trimming and without folding case (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:540-553), while the map matches ids without regard to case. A session that names 'Machine_V2' therefore lands on the machine_v2 row but the client omits the transcriber parameter and the vendor's default model answers. The resolver must hand the client the row's id, not the customer's spelling. Today's client serves any id its model gate does not recognise, including the deprecated low_cost and fusion, with the account's default streaming model and no warning (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:540-553), which is why native_model_handling is substituted.

reverie.notes: Registered in the plugin registry as reverie with the aliases reverie-ai, reverie_ai, reverie-stt and reverieinc (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1738-1741). Reverie has no model parameter, so default_model is null and the wildcard row is the only row. The gateway reads the session's model field as the customer's Reverie app id, which is why model_string is sensitive. Moving the app id into its own credential field is a precondition for any per-model row. The vendor offers a live WebSocket product next to its file product and publishes one language list shared by both, without stating coverage per product, but the gateway's streaming client cannot hold a call with more than one utterance as written, so the synchronous file product is recorded as a file transport; no release builds it, because the integration decisions place Reverie in no vendor wave. The only live contact with the vendor during the research was an unauthenticated request to the file endpoint, which returned HTTP 404 with the message 'REV-API-KEY header not found'. Nothing was transcribed, which is why the row says it was verified from documentation.

sarvam.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1714-1715. The standard factory matches only the exact id 'sarvam' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:457), so a session that uses an alias falls to the flat factory. default_model records what the code does today: an empty model becomes saarika:v2.5 (gateway/src/core/stt/sarvam/config.rs:26, 141-145). That id is deprecated and absent from the legacy socket's documented model list; the audit recommends changing the default to saaras:v4, and this field must change in the same commit. Sarvam has two generations of socket: the legacy one the gateway speaks (one final per utterance, no interim text) and a realtime one with partial transcripts and manual endpointing, for which the gateway has no client. No Sarvam model on sale is file-only, so file upload is a fallback. Rate limits, not price, bind a segmented path here: 60 requests per minute per account on the Starter tier. The streaming client accepts only 8 kHz and 16 kHz sessions (gateway/src/core/stt/sarvam/config.rs:317-322), so a /v1/realtime voice agent, whose speech-to-text leg is set to 24 kHz (gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:342), fails at setup with Sarvam today. The rows list two commit transports that no release builds, the realtime socket and a gateway-driven flush on the legacy socket. Both carry the adapter id planned_commit and are told apart by dialect.wire (sarvam_realtime_websocket and sarvam_legacy_websocket), because they differ in wire format and language notation.
