availability.note: Connection is not available to new customers from 15 July 2026; existing customers keep working and no end date is published.

sberdevices.notes: SberDevices SaluteSpeech. No model is file-only at the vendor (gRPC v2 streams with partial results and vendor end-of-utterance), but the gateway has no gRPC client for it, so every model needs the file-upload transport. The client registered today (gateway/src/core/stt/sberdevices/client.rs) is a synchronous REST client behind a 500 ms wall-clock timer. It is not a transport: when_unusable on each row records what a live session gets from it, and decisions section 5 keeps it, reported as known broken, until the file-upload transport is enabled. Today's client reads the session's model field as the OAuth scope, not as a model (gateway/src/core/stt/sberdevices/config.rs:297-302), so the map's model key only becomes meaningful once model and scope are separated. Until then the resolver must not use the session's model field as the lookup key for this provider: it holds a scope string or one of its short forms (PERS, PERSONAL, CORP, CORPORATE, B2B, LEGACY; config.rs:194-205). The acoustic model the customer asked for travels in extras["model"] on the standardized path (config.rs:351-356); that value, or 'general' when it is absent, is the right key. Otherwise a session that asks for callcenter through extras resolves to the default row and uploads at 16 kHz instead of 8 kHz. Today a live session still builds the legacy client, whose connect step requests an OAuth token before anything else (gateway/src/core/stt/sberdevices/client.rs:509-530); because the gateway's HTTP client ships a root list without the Russian Trusted Root CA (gateway/Cargo.toml:169), the session is expected to fail at setup on the certificate check (inferred, not run). Aliases differ by path: the standardized factory accepts sberdevices, sber_devices, sber, salutespeech and salute_speech (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:458); the plugin registry accepts sber, sber-devices, sber_devices, salutespeech, salute-speech and smartspeech (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1753-1756).

prerequisites.detail: The deployment's own base address, usually a private in-cluster address, must reach the speech-to-text leg through a trusted channel from the deployment record; today only the text-to-speech leg receives it (bud_legs.rs:654-664), and the client-settable endpoint override is refused for private addresses.

self_hosted.notes: The vendor id for a transcription server the operator runs and that speaks the OpenAI file-transcription request: POST {api_base}/audio/transcriptions, multipart. The four spellings are SELF_HOSTED_NAMES in gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:49-54, matched after trimming and lower-casing by is_self_hosted (:63-66); the module comment (:5-6) says budapp registers the source as waav_self_hosted and publishes vendor self_hosted. A WaaV Infer engine published through Bud is expected to arrive under this id as well; that is an inference (no other vendor id for it is registered, and the engine's route fits the URL join), and how such an engine is published is still an open decision. The id is recognised but not registered for speech-to-text: the plugin registry has no speech-to-text entry for it (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1666-1809; only the text-to-speech plugin at :1818-1819), create_stt_standard has no arm for it, and a live call that names such a deployment is refused today with the codes unsupported_deployment and stt_not_streaming (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and :815-826). Integration decisions addendum A1 keeps those two codes for a self-hosted deployment the segmented engine does not cover, until the Bud-side check on them is answered. The upload route works through a passthrough (gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:2789-2901). default_model is null because the model always comes from the deployment record. Today's leg code sends config.stt.model when set, otherwise voice_table.model (bud_legs.rs:216-226); the plan sends voice_table.model and uses config.stt.model only to look the row up (deployment_model_source). The vendor id does not say which server software is behind the address, so rows state only what holds across servers, and a deployment override selects a named profile from profiles.json when the operator knows more. Do not reuse the stale alias self-hosted that gateway/src/core/stt/infer.rs:24 still lists for the WaaV Infer stub; it belongs to this provider.

speechmatics.notes: Registered as speechmatics with aliases speech-matics and speech_matics (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:185-201, :1719), plus speechmatics-stt in the static dispatch table (gateway/src/plugin/dispatch.rs:294). Only the spelling speechmatics reaches the standardized factory (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:461); the aliases take the flat factory, which drops the standardized features (standard.rs:476), so the resolver must normalise the provider id before lookup. default_model is standard because the vendor uses it when no model is sent, and the client sends none for an empty model (gateway/src/core/stt/speechmatics/config.rs:522-524). The client's model gate is a substring match (config.rs:526-531): any id containing 'standard' or 'enhanced' selects an operating point. The short aliases std, enh and high (config.rs:100-101) are model aliases of the standard and enhanced rows, and the placeholder nova-3, which the client reads as unset (config.rs:485, :522), is covered by key_normalisation; the substring rule has no field, so the resolver must apply it before lookup or those sessions fall to the provider default row. Every other id, including melia-1, oak-1 and linden-1, is refused by name at construction (config.rs:536-540). The melia-1 and oak-1 rows are the least stable facts in this file: the vendor planned a realtime release for October 2026, so they carry a re-check date and need a probe with a key. The batch hosts are eu1, us1 and au1 (eu2 and us2 also exist, for Enterprise failover only). Batch jobs are bound to the regional host that created them, melia-1 and oak-1 exist only on the EU1 and US1 hosts (a region constraint on their batch transports), and the client can only dial the EU realtime host (config.rs:652). The batch service stores audio and transcripts for 7 days unless the job is deleted; the realtime socket stores nothing.

tencent.notes: Registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1778-1781; dispatched at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:464-465. MODEL KEY: the model id is Tencent's engine id (engine_model_type on the socket, engine_type on flash, EngSerViceType on SentenceRecognition). Language is chosen by the engine id; there is no separate language parameter. An empty model resolves to 16k_zh (gateway/src/core/stt/tencent/config.rs:39, fallback at :173). Ids are case-sensitive on the wire (16k_zh-TW, 16k_zh-PY, Hy-ASR-3.0-preview); match.model keeps the vendor's spelling, which is what a non-native adapter sends. SITES: the two synchronous file APIs (flash and SentenceRecognition) exist on the China site only, recorded as the region constraint 'china' on those transports; the international site offers the real-time socket and an asynchronous job. Streaming concurrency differs by site (200 connections per account on the China site, 50 for real-time version 2 engines, 20 on the international site); each socket transport's rates entry records one figure and its note says which. STREAMING CLIENT (adapter native, known_broken; read from code and vendor documentation, never run against the vendor; all paths under gateway/src/core/stt/tencent/): (1) messages.rs:158-165 treats slice_type 1 as a finished segment and client.rs:430-436 sets is_final for it, but the vendor defines 1 as an unstable in-progress result and 2 as the only stable one, so every growing partial reaches turn-taking as a final transcript. (2) Hang-up sends a WebSocket Close frame (client.rs:118, :177) and never the vendor end message {"type":"end"}; is_speech_final is set from final==1 (client.rs:441) but the vendor's final message carries no result, so it is never emitted. (3) The signed URL and voice_id are built once (client.rs:494) and reused on every reconnect (client.rs:544); the vendor voids a voice_id after any interruption. (4) Vendor sentence detection (needvad) follows the customer's vad_events feature (config.rs:859-861), so vad_events=false silently turns vendor endpointing off. (5) Unknown engine ids become 16k_zh (config.rs:173) and STTConfig.language is never read, so a request that sets only a language runs Mandarin. (6) Hot words are sent as Base64 JSON (signature.rs:276-285) where the vendor expects 'word|weight' pairs. The repository mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:420-431) sends result and final in one message, a shape the vendor page does not show, so its passing test covers none of this. FILE UPLOAD (not implemented; flash through adapter regional_rest, SentenceRecognition as planned_file, which no release builds): batch_provider_supported (gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:839-844) lists only deepgram, assemblyai, openai and elevenlabs, and the Tencent feature row has batch_builder None (gateway/src/core/capabilities.rs:362-365). The two interfaces are told apart by dialect.wire: tencent_flash and tencent_sentence_recognition. Neither returns a confidence, a no-speech probability or a detected language, so quality filtering can only drop empty text. Concurrency limits are per Tencent account, so the limiter must be shared by every call on the account. Byte limits the vendor states as '100 MB' and '3 MB' are recorded with the decimal reading, the lower one. STATE TODAY: the streaming client is the native transport, enabled from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, and reported as known broken in ready.stt rather than refused (integration decisions, section 15); each native transport carries its defect. The file transport (regional_rest) is enabled from Release 5, wider vendor coverage and hardening, and only after a live probe with a real key (decisions section 12). Until then a model the gateway has no working path for is refused or warned as its when_unusable says. Segmentation is required only for 16k_zh-PY and 16k_zh_dialect, and only for China-site accounts. config/pricing.rs has no Tencent entries, so rows carry no pricing_key. LIVE TESTING: the research machine could not resolve asr.cloud.tencent.com or asr.tencentcloudapi.com, so no defect and no vendor fact in these rows was checked against the live service; that needs a host inside mainland China or one whose DNS resolves the Tencent API hosts.

tinkoff.notes: T-Bank (formerly Tinkoff) VoiceKit. One recognition service with four methods and no published model ids; the row key 'default' is the gateway's placeholder and is never sent on the wire (the request the gateway builds has no model field, gateway/src/core/stt/tinkoff/messages.rs:268-295). The vendor streams natively (bidirectional gRPC with interim results and its own endpointing), so segmentation is only a fallback, and no release builds it. The existing streaming client is expected to fail against the vendor on four counts (trust root, authentication, response field number, response nesting; inferred from code reading and the certificate chain, not run). It stays the session's client from Release 0 and is reported as known broken (gateway_client.defect), because decisions section 15 reports a broken native client instead of refusing it. Its connect step opens the TLS channel first (gateway/src/core/stt/tinkoff/provider.rs:344-345, grpc.rs:49-61), so the session is expected to fail at setup on the certificate check, before authentication is attempted (inferred, not run). Besides the trust root, every transport needs JWT authentication ('authorization: Bearer <JWT>'). LongRunningRecognize is an asynchronous job of up to 24 hours and must never be used for calls. Aliases: only the literal 'tinkoff' reaches the standardized factory (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:467); the registry aliases (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1748-1751) take the flat path. Public examples are Russian only.

viettel-ai.notes: Registry id and aliases: gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1804-1805; the standardized factory that live sessions use accepts viettel-ai, viettel_ai, viettelai and viettel (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:468-470). The vendor does stream (a documented WebSocket), but the gateway cannot: its only client is an HTTP client that buffers the call until 9.6 MB, hang-up or a client commit (client.rs:388-423), and it is not a transport. Nothing works today: that client posts to a host the vendor no longer controls and misreads the vendor's current reply, so the provider cannot serve a call or a file. Security fix needed regardless of this work: the speech-to-text and text-to-speech clients send the customer token and call audio to viettelgroup.ai (gateway/src/core/stt/viettel_ai/config.rs:40; gateway/src/core/tts/viettel_ai/config.rs:41, :44), a domain that the registry shows was newly registered through a privacy proxy on 2025-11-14 and is no longer the vendor's. The server has no credential mapping for this provider (gateway/src/config/mod.rs:679). Vietnamese only.

prerequisites.detail: The engine binds loopback with no authentication by default (port 8080), so the gateway reaches it only through a trusted, operator-configured private base address from the deployment record.

waav-infer.notes: WaaV Infer is the operator's own inference engine. The gateway has a distinct id for it: INFER_STT_PROVIDER_ID = "waav-infer" (gateway/src/core/stt/infer.rs:23), which is also the id the speech-to-speech realtime adapter reports (gateway/src/core/realtime/infer/protocol.rs:130-132). For speech-to-text the adapter is a stub whose connect always fails (infer.rs:59-65) and it is deliberately left out of the plugin registry (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:2096-2130), so a session that names this provider gets the registry's unknown-provider error today. The aliases are those at infer.rs:24 without self-hosted, which that line still lists but which now names the self_hosted provider. Through Bud a WaaV Infer engine is expected to be published as vendor self_hosted with a base address ending in /v1 (an inference; the publishing route is an open decision), and then the self_hosted rows apply, with the profile waav-infer-file when the operator declares it; these rows exist so that a session naming waav-infer directly resolves to a stated answer instead of the global default. default_model is null: the engine hosts one speech-to-text model per process and an empty model means that model. The speech-to-speech realtime provider is a separate path that these rows do not touch.

yandex.notes: Yandex SpeechKit. The vendor streams only over gRPC (v3 recommended, v2 legacy; no WebSocket) and the gateway has no gRPC client for it, so every model that can serve a call needs the file-upload transport. The client registered today (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs) is a synchronous REST client behind a 500 ms wall-clock timer. It is not a transport: when_unusable on each row records what a live session gets from it, and decisions section 5 keeps it, reported as known broken, until the file-upload transport is enabled. It is billed one 15 s unit for each half-second piece and ends a turn on every piece, so keeping it is costly and unusable for conversation. Aliases: the standardized factory accepts yandex, yandex-speechkit, yandex_speechkit and speechkit (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:471); the plugin registry also accepts yandex-stt and yandex_stt (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1744-1746), which today miss the standardized path. Gateway-side model aliases (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:187-201) are not wire strings: 'default' is a model_aliases entry of the general row, and 'rc' and 'realtime' of the general:rc row. 'batch' means the gateway's own id 'deferred' and has no alias entry (an alias cannot sit on the 'deferred*' pattern row), so the resolver must still rewrite it to 'deferred' before lookup; otherwise it falls to the provider default row and would be sent to the vendor as the 'topic' value. Today's client replaces any id it does not know with 'general' (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/config.rs:291-295). The API host uses a publicly trusted certificate chain, unlike Sber and T-Bank.

gateway_client.notes: This is what the client does today with any id it does not know: the id becomes Custom (config.rs:176) and is sent a run-task on the inference socket (config.rs:707-717), whether or not the vendor serves that id there. It is listed first and usable from Release 0, groundwork and honest refusal, so that unknown ids behave exactly as they do today; the file upload behind it is chosen only with transcription_mode segmented. Protocol: run-task on /api-ws/v1/inference, binary audio frames, result-generated events; a result is final when the vendor sets sentence_end. Defects that do not stop a call: the client sends semantic_punctuation_enabled=true by default (messages.rs:436), which the vendor says switches off silence-based segmentation and makes max_sentence_silence (the gateway's endpointing_ms mapping) inert; confidence is hard-coded to 1.0 and word times are dropped (client.rs:569-575); the host is the Beijing legacy domain unless an endpoint override is set (config.rs:574); connect() reports success before the vendor's task-started arrives (client.rs:230-232).

segment_profile.rationale: The 8 s request timeout is the audit's provisional budget, not a measurement: the vendor publishes no response time for the synchronous file interface. Replace it with the measured 99th percentile plus a margin after the first run with a key. billing.notes: Nothing is known about an id with no exact row. min_billed_ms is the largest minimum among this provider's file models (qwen3-asr-flash bills at least one second per request), so an unknown id that is uploaded is merged and metered conservatively; it says nothing about a stream. gateway_client.notes: Nothing to reuse: gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:839-844 supports only deepgram, assemblyai, openai and elevenlabs, and gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:102-109 has no DashScope vendor. Today the client accepts this id, falls to Custom (config.rs:176) and sends a run-task on the streaming socket (config.rs:707-717), where a file-only model cannot work; connect() reports success before the vendor answers (client.rs:230-232), so the failure arrives later as a per-audio error. Request: POST <host>/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation with header X-DashScope-SSE: disable, the audio as a data: URI in a content part of type input_audio, and parameters.format=wav plus parameters.sample_rate=16000. Response text at output.text, word times in output.sentence.words[] (no confidence), billed seconds in usage.duration; the vendor warns there is no choices field. Server-sent events give intermediate text only for audio of at least one minute.

segment_profile.rationale: The 8 s request timeout is the audit's provisional budget, not a measurement: the vendor publishes no response time for the synchronous file interface. Replace it with the measured 99th percentile plus a margin after the first run with a key. Every other setting stays at the gateway default: a 25 s segment is about 1.07 MB after base64, far below the 10 MB limit, and no per-request minimum billing is documented for this model, so short segments need not be merged. Two uploads in flight per session is kept, but the account-wide request limit needs a limiter shared by all sessions.

gateway_client.notes: This id is not in the client's model list; it falls to Custom (config.rs:176) and is sent the same Paraformer-shaped run-task. The model is 8 kHz, but the client forces the declared sample rate to 8000 only for the two Paraformer 8 kHz variants (config.rs:200-205, :583-587); for this id it declares the session's rate, so a 16 kHz session would be mis-declared to an 8 kHz model (inferred). Never exercised with this model. Protocol: run-task on /api-ws/v1/inference, binary audio frames, result-generated events; a result is final when the vendor sets sentence_end. Defects that do not stop a call: the client sends semantic_punctuation_enabled=true by default (messages.rs:436), which the vendor says switches off silence-based segmentation and makes max_sentence_silence (the gateway's endpointing_ms mapping) inert; confidence is hard-coded to 1.0 and word times are dropped (client.rs:569-575); the host is the Beijing legacy domain unless an endpoint override is set (config.rs:574); connect() reports success before the vendor's task-started arrives (client.rs:230-232).

Today the client accepts this id, falls to Custom (config.rs:176) and sends a run-task on the streaming socket (config.rs:707-717), where a file-only model cannot work; connect() reports success before the vendor answers (client.rs:230-232), so the failure arrives later as a per-audio error. Request: POST <host>/api/v1/services/aigc/multimodal-generation/generation with header X-DashScope-SSE: disable, the audio as a data: URI in a content part of type input_audio, and parameters.format=wav plus parameters.sample_rate=16000. Response text at output.text, word times in output.sentence.words[] (no confidence), billed seconds in usage.duration; the vendor warns there is no choices field. Server-sent events give intermediate text only for audio of at least one minute.

segment_profile.rationale: The 8 s request timeout is the audit's provisional budget, not a measurement: the vendor publishes no response time for the synchronous file interface. Replace it with the measured 99th percentile plus a margin after the first run with a key. Every other setting stays at the gateway default: a 25 s segment is about 1.07 MB after base64, far below the 10 MB limit, and no per-request minimum billing is documented for this model, so short segments need not be merged. Two uploads in flight per session is kept, but the account-wide request limit needs a limiter shared by all sessions.

gateway_client.defect: The gateway's Qwen realtime client does not match the vendor's documented protocol. The vendor's final-transcript event carries emotion as a plain string; the client declares it as an object, so the event fails to parse and the transcript is dropped (found by reading the types and the vendor page, not executed). The session.update message also differs from the documented shape. Correct the parser and add a unit test with the vendor's sample event before enabling.
gateway_client.notes: Protocol: session.update on /api-ws/v1/realtime?model=<id>, base64 audio appends, vendor voice detection ends each utterance. Evidence of the mismatch: emotion is declared as {tag, confidence} (messages.rs:222-224, :238-246) while the vendor sends a string; a parse failure is only logged (client.rs:546-548); no test fixture contains emotion. session.update nests sample_rate under input_audio_transcription (vendor: session.sample_rate), defaults the threshold to 0.5 (vendor 0.2) and announces manual mode as type 'manual' (vendor: turn_detection null) (messages.rs:85-109, client.rs:477-496). The vendor's interim event conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.text is not handled (client.rs:523-545), which is why interim_results is 'none' although the vendor offers live interims. The gateway sends silence_duration_ms 400 (config.rs:57); the vendor default is 800. Covered only by message-shape unit tests; no mock or live run exists for this path. The transport stays usable from Release 0 with the defect reported in ready.stt (decisions section 15), so a default-configured session keeps today's behaviour: it connects and, on paper, returns no transcript.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented. No AmiVoice file-request code exists in the gateway (gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:839-844 and gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:102-123 do not include AmiVoice). The vendor serves every engine on its socket, so file upload is a fallback, not a requirement.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/recognize (the vendor keeps a log) or https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/nolog/recognize (no log; the path also selects the price). Multipart fields u (API key), d (engine id, optionally followed by key=value settings, percent-encoded with %20 for spaces), then the audio part a, which must be last because fields after it are ignored. A WAV header is detected automatically, so the format field c is omitted. The gateway has only unused URL constants for this endpoint (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:42, 45). The vendor documents a single HTTP 200 response and reports failure in the body's one-character code, so the adapter must classify the body itself: an empty code is success; 'o' means rejected or no speech and is an empty transcript; '+', '-', '%', '^' and 'x' are request or configuration faults that must not be retried ('^' is documented for the asynchronous interface only); 'b', '!', '<', '#', '$', '?' and 'c' may be retried. The code '>' is disputed. The vendor's page lists it with the client errors for which 'retrying will yield the same result' and says it is what an upload without audio data returns; the same page's code table describes it as a failure to send audio inside the vendor's servers; the fact-check lists it as a retry candidate. Retry it at most once, and never for an upload the gateway knows to be empty. The response has no interim text. The vendor runs its own speech detector on the upload, force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds and ends the request after 50 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout). The vendor's only latency statement for this interface is that conversion finishes 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent, at the latest'; no percentile is published. All processing is in Japan. The vendor's asynchronous job API takes tens of seconds to minutes just to start a job and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

segment_profile.rationale: Two deviations from the gateway defaults. Maximum segment 14 seconds instead of 25: the synchronous interface force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds at an arbitrary point, so the gateway must cut at a pause before that. Request timeout 15 seconds: the vendor's only bound for this interface is 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent', which for a 14 second segment plus padding is about 15 seconds; it is an upper bound from a vendor statement, not a measured figure, and should be replaced by a measured value. Container, 16 kHz rate, pre-roll, trailing silence and two uploads in flight stay at the defaults: silence is not billed and no concurrency limit is published.

gateway_client.notes: The only test runs against an in-repo mock that answers on any binary frame, so it cannot see the missing prefix (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:660-704). Whether the client fails against the live service was not tested; both sides were read and no key was available. As written, the client forwards each chunk at once as a binary frame, turns vendor U events into interim results about once a second and turns each vendor A event into a result with is_final and is_speech_final both true (client.rs:557-577; messages.rs:210-213). The vendor's speech-start and speech-end events are only logged (client.rs:545-551). The vendor's own detector ends an utterance after 550 ms of silence by default and force-finalises any utterance at 15 seconds. Other defects found by reading: with the header-format names, 16 kHz raw audio works only through a vendor fallback and any other rate is decoded at the wrong rate; the start command, which contains the API key, is written to the debug log (client.rs:155); a start error containing 'auth' is reported as a bad key although the vendor uses the same message for a wrong engine name (client.rs:203-216); a final with empty text is dropped without reading its error code (client.rs:568-577). The vendor disconnects after 600 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout) and after 60 seconds without traffic; a session may last 24 hours.
gateway_client.defect: Known broken: the client does not match the vendor's wire protocol. Audio frames and the keep-alive frame are sent without the mandatory first byte 0x70 ('p') (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/client.rs:266-268, 335-336), and raw PCM is declared with the format names 8K and 16K, which the vendor reserves for audio that has a file header (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:403-404, 419-425). Treat it as working only after both are fixed and one live call has returned a transcript.

billing.notes: Billed per second, and only for the speech the vendor's own detector finds: silence is not charged, on the socket or on upload. The vendor states there is no minimum fee per request. Speech that is detected but then rejected as filler or noise is still billed. Monthly usage is rounded down to whole seconds; there is a monthly floor of 50 yen (no charge below it) and 60 free minutes a month. The price depends on the engine tier and on whether the logging endpoint is used. There is no AmiVoice entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: Default for an AmiVoice engine id the map has never seen. Every engine the vendor offers streams, but the gateway's streaming client does not match the vendor protocol. File upload is listed first, where the builders placed it as the path a wrong guess can survive, but no release builds an AmiVoice file transcriber, so that transport is never enabled and such a session gets the streaming client, known broken, reported and not refused. The resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. Six ids that the gateway itself accepts are not in the vendor's engine table and land on this row: -a-finance, -a-insurance, -a-finance-input, -a-insurance-input, -a-name-input and -a-address-input (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:116-161). They have no row because the map has no way to mark an id as known to be invalid; the code must replace them with the vendor ids. Today the client turns any unrecognised string into -a-general without warning (config.rs:563); the provider's native_model_handling (substituted) makes the resolver warn with stt_model_substituted instead.

gateway_client.notes: The only test runs against an in-repo mock that answers on any binary frame, so it cannot see the missing prefix (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:660-704). Whether the client fails against the live service was not tested; both sides were read and no key was available. As written, the client forwards each chunk at once as a binary frame, turns vendor U events into interim results about once a second and turns each vendor A event into a result with is_final and is_speech_final both true (client.rs:557-577; messages.rs:210-213). The vendor's speech-start and speech-end events are only logged (client.rs:545-551). The vendor's own detector ends an utterance after 550 ms of silence by default and force-finalises any utterance at 15 seconds. Other defects found by reading: with the header-format names, 16 kHz raw audio works only through a vendor fallback and any other rate is decoded at the wrong rate; the start command, which contains the API key, is written to the debug log (client.rs:155); a start error containing 'auth' is reported as a bad key although the vendor uses the same message for a wrong engine name (client.rs:203-216); a final with empty text is dropped without reading its error code (client.rs:568-577). The vendor disconnects after 600 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout) and after 60 seconds without traffic; a session may last 24 hours.
gateway_client.defect: Known broken: the client does not match the vendor's wire protocol. Audio frames and the keep-alive frame are sent without the mandatory first byte 0x70 ('p') (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/client.rs:266-268, 335-336), and raw PCM is declared with the format names 8K and 16K, which the vendor reserves for audio that has a file header (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:403-404, 419-425). Treat it as working only after both are fixed and one live call has returned a transcript.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. The vendor documents that after the client sends the end command 'e', a new start command 's' may be sent on the same connection. The gateway would send 'e' when its own detector reports end of speech, collect the final results up to the vendor's 'e' response, then send 's' again. Decoding runs while the caller is still speaking, so the wait after end of speech should be shorter than an upload, and the gateway owns the turn boundary. Nothing here has been measured.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/recognize (the vendor keeps a log) or https://acp-api.amivoice.com/v1/nolog/recognize (no log; the path also selects the price). Multipart fields u (API key), d (engine id, optionally followed by key=value settings, percent-encoded with %20 for spaces), then the audio part a, which must be last because fields after it are ignored. A WAV header is detected automatically, so the format field c is omitted. The gateway has only unused URL constants for this endpoint (gateway/src/core/stt/amivoice/config.rs:42, 45). The vendor documents a single HTTP 200 response and reports failure in the body's one-character code, so the adapter must classify the body itself: an empty code is success; 'o' means rejected or no speech and is an empty transcript; '+', '-', '%', '^' and 'x' are request or configuration faults that must not be retried ('^' is documented for the asynchronous interface only); 'b', '!', '<', '#', '$', '?' and 'c' may be retried. The code '>' is disputed. The vendor's page lists it with the client errors for which 'retrying will yield the same result' and says it is what an upload without audio data returns; the same page's code table describes it as a failure to send audio inside the vendor's servers; the fact-check lists it as a retry candidate. Retry it at most once, and never for an upload the gateway knows to be empty. The response has no interim text. The vendor runs its own speech detector on the upload, force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds and ends the request after 50 seconds without detected speech (the value recorded as the timeout). The vendor's only latency statement for this interface is that conversion finishes 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent, at the latest'; no percentile is published. All processing is in Japan. The vendor's asynchronous job API takes tens of seconds to minutes just to start a job and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

segment_profile.rationale: Two deviations from the gateway defaults. Maximum segment 14 seconds instead of 25: the synchronous interface force-finalises a single utterance at 15 seconds at an arbitrary point, so the gateway must cut at a pause before that. Request timeout 15 seconds: the vendor's only bound for this interface is 'within 1x the duration of the audio sent', which for a 14 second segment plus padding is about 15 seconds; it is an upper bound from a vendor statement, not a measured figure, and should be replaced by a measured value. Container, 16 kHz rate, pre-roll, trailing silence and two uploads in flight stay at the defaults: silence is not billed and no concurrency limit is published.

billing.notes: Billed per second, and only for the speech the vendor's own detector finds: silence is not charged, on the socket or on upload. The vendor states there is no minimum fee per request. Speech that is detected but then rejected as filler or noise is still billed. Monthly usage is rounded down to whole seconds; there is a monthly floor of 50 yen (no charge below it) and 60 free minutes a month. The price depends on the engine tier and on whether the logging endpoint is used. There is no AmiVoice entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: The model id 'standard' is a gateway identifier, not a string Amazon accepts: Amazon Transcribe has no base-model parameter and products are chosen by API operation. 'standard' is the name the gateway's price table already uses, and an empty model resolves to this row. The only model-like vendor field is a customer-trained custom language model name, which the gateway holds in its configuration and never sends. Amazon Transcribe has no request-and-response file call: the only file interface is StartTranscriptionJob, an asynchronous job that reads the audio from an S3 bucket in the same region and writes the transcript to S3. It is deliberately not listed as a transport, so segmented mode is not available for this provider. Language and region decide whether a call can be served, not the model. Eighteen language codes exist only in the batch API and can never be streamed; they are the language constraint of the streaming transport. A further 45 languages cannot be streamed in af-south-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-5, ap-southeast-7 and cn-northwest-1, which a constraint cannot express because it cannot combine a language with a region. Decisions section 12 refuses a batch-only language at setup; addendum A7 places that refusal in Release 3.

Every Azure OpenAI model served by the /audio interface is file-only, so file upload is right for all of them. It is wrong only for a deployment of a realtime-only base model (gpt-live-transcribe, gpt-realtime-whisper), where each upload would be rejected by Azure; such a deployment must declare its base model. Restore the gateway defaults (upload at each pause, two in flight) only for a deployment whose quota increase is confirmed.

gateway_client.notes: How the session must work: open the socket with intent=transcription; send session.update with session.type set to transcription, input format audio/pcm at 24 kHz (the gateway must resample from the caller's rate), the transcription model, and turn_detection null; append base64 audio continuously; when the gateway's own voice detector decides the utterance has ended, send input_audio_buffer.commit. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta while the caller speaks and as ...completed after the commit. Completions for different turns may arrive out of order and must be matched by item_id. A commit on an empty buffer is an error. The live models reject the vendor's own voice detection, which is why the gateway owns endpointing here. The intent=transcription query is what the gateway relay, Pipecat and LiveKit dial and what Microsoft's sample uses; it is absent from OpenAI's own pages. The language and context fields are left out of this profile because they differ by model (languages and keywords on gpt-live-transcribe, language and no prompt on gpt-realtime-whisper) and a profile cannot see the model. On Azure the socket is wss://{resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription with an api-key header and no api-version; the deployment name goes in session.audio.input.transcription.model. Microsoft's sample sets turn_detection to none and sends the commit itself at 24 kHz. A session lasts at most 60 minutes, so a longer call needs a reconnect.

The gateway sends api-version 2025-04-01-preview unless the deployment sets provider_params.api_version (self_hosted.rs:115; gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1557-1561). The existing code has a 300 second deadline, returns the body unparsed and has no circuit breaker, so only its request half can be reused. Azure ignores stream=true for this model, so text never arrives in pieces. verbose_json is accepted and Microsoft says it returns per-segment probabilities, but the field names are not spelled out on the Azure pages, so no quality signal is claimed until a live response has been read.

segment_profile.rationale: Azure's default quota for the speech-to-text audio API is 3 requests per minute. One upload per caller turn is the most that quota can carry, so segments are held and uploaded once per turn, one at a time. Restore the gateway defaults (upload at each pause, two in flight) only for a deployment whose quota increase is confirmed.

when_unusable.code_ref: gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 (code unsupported_deployment, /ws and DAG legs) and :815-826 (code stt_not_streaming, voice-agent legs)

refusal.text: Azure OpenAI serves this model by transcribing one uploaded audio file per request; it has no live streaming interface. This gateway does not yet serve it on a live call for this deployment. Use the deployment for file transcription, choose a streaming transcription deployment for the call, or ask the operator to enable segmented speech-to-text for this deployment.

transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls does not exist yet. The existing Bhashini client buffers the whole call in memory and uploads it once, when the client is disconnected (at hang-up, or earlier if the caller's application sends an explicit end-of-audio message), so it produces no transcript while the caller is speaking.

latency.notes: Not measured. The vendor publishes no latency for the compute call and no credentials were available to measure it.

gateway_client.notes: There is no per-utterance upload. Request code that can be reused does exist: PipelineComputeRequest::new_asr builds the JSON body and send_audio_to_compute posts it, but today it runs only once, at disconnect, on the whole buffered call. The exchange has two steps. A pipeline configuration call returns the upload address, the name and value of the authorisation header, and the service id; then one synchronous JSON request carries the audio as base64 text in inputData.audio[0].audioContent. It is not multipart, and a full 25 s segment is about 1.05 MiB of JSON. The language travels as config.language.sourceLanguage and the format as audioFormat and samplingRate, which must match the audio. Before reuse: build one pooled HTTP client instead of one per request (client.rs:412-421); replace the three attempts of 60 s each (client.rs:54-63); accept null for output and audio in the response, because the vendor's documented sample has audio set to null and the present structs reject that (messages.rs:354-359); send post-processors in the compute request, where the vendor reads them; and stop reporting a fixed confidence of 0.95 (client.rs:377). The adapter must not send the vendor's voice-activity pre-processor, because the gateway has already cut the audio.

transports.disabled_reason: No gateway client exists for the vendor's Socket.IO speech recognition interface (wss://dhruva-api.bhashini.gov.in), and the vendor does not say which service ids it serves. gateway_client.notes: Listed so that the map records that the vendor does offer a live interface; routing must follow what the gateway can do, which is nothing on this transport. The gateway has no Socket.IO dependency. Facts from the vendor's page and its own Java client: audio is 8 kHz 16-bit mono PCM; the client sends a start event carrying the service id, waits for ready, then sends data events; the server sends response events at a configured interval (responseFrequencyInSecs). gateway_client.notes: Cartesia built this socket for a client that decides where the utterance ends: the client streams audio and sends the text command finalize when its own voice detector says the caller stopped; the server returns the remaining transcript and then a flush_done acknowledgment. The vendor calls sending finalize crucial for low latency. Three things are missing. First, a caller for the existing finalize method (client.rs:592-608): it should be driven by the gateway's own detector reporting the end of speech. Second, the command must go out as bare text; the client serialises it as a JSON-quoted string (messages.rs:45-57). Third, final chunks are deltas and must be joined without trimming, and the turn should end on flush_done or on the turn controller's decision, not on every final chunk (messages.rs:104-111). The vendor warns that finalizing in the middle of speech causes transcription errors, and that the server waits for more audio rather than assuming silence when frames stop arriving.

gateway_client.defect: The client never sends finalize, so Cartesia's slower silence fallback ends each utterance, and it marks every final chunk as the end of the caller's turn although each chunk's text is a delta, so one utterance can end the turn more than once. It also differs from the current documentation in its authentication parameter, pinned API version and command format, with an effect nobody has probed.
gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against in-repo mock sockets (a mock end-to-end test and a reconnect test); the evidence records no run against Cartesia. Each caller chunk is written at once as a raw binary frame (client.rs:115-121) and every transcript event is forwarded, interim or final (client.rs:386-392). The client never sends Cartesia's finalize command (the method that would is unused, client.rs:592-608), so Cartesia's silence fallback ends each utterance. Every final chunk is marked as the end of the caller's turn (messages.rs:104-111), although the vendor's text is a delta since the previous final chunk, so one utterance can end the turn more than once. Confidence is invented, 1.0 for a final and 0.0 for an interim, because Cartesia returns none (messages.rs:109). The client differs from Cartesia's current documentation in three ways whose effect is unknown: it authenticates with an api_key query parameter (config.rs:279-280) where the documentation now lists a header or an access-token parameter; it pins API version 2025-04-16 (config.rs:139) where the current version is 2026-08-14 and structured error codes start at 2026-03-01; and it ends the session with the JSON-quoted text "done" (client.rs:82-91, messages.rs:45-57) where the documentation specifies the bare text close. If Cartesia has stopped accepting any of these, this client does not work today; probe it against the vendor before relying on it.

billing.notes: Nothing is known about how an unrecognised Cartesia id is billed. Known models are billed in credits per second of audio on the socket, silence included.

gateway_client.notes: Cartesia's file endpoint is POST /stt: a multipart request with a file part, a model field that must name a model of the ink-whisper family and a language field (default en, no detection). It needs an Authorization header and a Cartesia-Version header and returns one JSON body with the text, the audio duration and, on request, word times. It is synchronous: no job and no polling. It returns no confidence of any kind, so a quality filter can use only an empty-transcript check, the gateway detector's own measure of speech and a list of phrases the model is known to invent. It takes no prompt and no vocabulary. The gateway has no Cartesia entry among its file-upload vendors (batch.rs:839-844; prerecorded.rs:116-123), so a file sent to the gateway's upload route for a Cartesia deployment is replayed over the streaming socket (standard.rs:514-522). The existing driver sends once, when the session disconnects, and then drops its callbacks (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); it uses a 300 s timeout and an HTTP/1.1 pool with a 90 s idle limit (prerecorded.rs:72, 177-185), and its parser marks every result as the end of the caller's turn (prerecorded.rs:897). None of that suits a live turn.

billing.notes: Only the uploaded seconds are billed, per second with no minimum. Deepgram's pre-recorded prices differ from its streaming prices.

Deepgram quotes prices per minute and bills per second of audio with no minimum; its pricing page says a 14 second file is billed as exactly 14 seconds. This describes the first transport, the streaming socket, on which the gateway forwards every frame including silence; the evidence does not say in so many words that silence on a stream is billed, so bills_silence is left unknown. The pricing_key deepgram:enhanced is an existing entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs. The file transport carries its own billing block.

gateway_client.notes: The client was exercised against Deepgram's live socket by key-gated tests that round-trip synthesised speech through it with nova-2 and nova-3 (gateway/tests/deepgram_live_e2e.rs:251-289), and Deepgram streaming was timed live for the gateway's latency analysis of 2026-06-05 (WaaV/LATENCY_ANALYSIS.md:18). The tests are marked ignore and continuous integration does not run them. This model id itself has not been exercised live; it uses the same client and differs only in the model query value. Each caller chunk is forwarded at once as one binary frame (deepgram.rs:950-957). Interim results are on. Deepgram decides where an utterance ends: the client asks for endpointing after 200 ms of silence by default (deepgram.rs:154, 520-523) and maps the vendor's speech_final flag to is_speech_final (deepgram.rs:684-690). The model id is written into the request unchecked (deepgram.rs:486-491).

context_params.note: Nova-2 and older models; Nova-3 replaced it with keyterm.

gateway_client.notes: Deepgram's Finalize message makes the server process buffered audio at once and return the final transcript. The client already recognises the from_finalize flag on a response (deepgram.rs:694-696) but nothing sends the message. Sending it when the gateway's own voice detector reports the end of speech would return the final without waiting for Deepgram's silence timer. This is an optional latency lever: Deepgram's own endpointing already ends utterances on this socket.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented. No per-utterance file adapter exists for live sessions; the Deepgram request builder and response parser serve the upload routes only. This model streams, so the file endpoint is a fallback, not a requirement.

latency.notes: Deepgram publishes no latency for the file endpoint on short audio; its latency guide covers streaming only. Must be measured before this transport is enabled.

Enterprise starts at 200.

context_params.note: Nova-2 and older models; Nova-3 replaced it with keyterm.

gateway_client.notes: No code takes one finished utterance and returns one transcript during a live session. The pieces to extract exist: a request builder for POST /v1/listen (batch.rs:346-353) and a response parser, today reached only from the two file-upload routes (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:223-225 and 607-610). The existing driver sends once, when the session disconnects, and then drops its callbacks (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); it uses a 300 s timeout and an HTTP/1.1 pool with a 90 s idle limit (prerecorded.rs:72, 177-185), and its parser marks every result as the end of the caller's turn (prerecorded.rs:897). None of that suits a live turn.

billing.notes: Only the uploaded seconds are billed, per second with no minimum. Deepgram's pre-recorded prices differ from its streaming prices.

Deepgram quotes prices per minute and bills per second of audio with no minimum; its pricing page says a 14 second file is billed as exactly 14 seconds. This describes the first transport, the streaming socket, on which the gateway forwards every frame including silence; the evidence does not say in so many words that silence on a stream is billed, so bills_silence is left unknown. There is no entry for this model in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, and lookups there are exact (pricing.rs:466-469), so metering reports no price until one is added. The file transport carries its own billing block.

provenance.notes: This model streams on wss /v1/listen, which is what a live call uses today and continues to use. The second transport, a gateway-driven Finalize on the same socket, and the third, Deepgram's synchronous file endpoint POST /v1/listen, are listed because the vendor offers them; neither is built. No release builds the Finalize transport. The file transport is enabled from Release 3, default on, and is used only when a session asks for segmented transcription, because the streaming client stays first. limits.rates holds only concurrency limits because Deepgram limits concurrent requests, not requests per unit of time. Deepgram labels this model family legacy and says it remains available at unchanged rates for existing deployments; no retirement date is published, so the status is legacy. This is the specification's spelling of a Base-family model; Deepgram's documentation tables spell the same models with a 'base-' prefix. Only the specification spelling has an exact row.

gateway_client.notes: The client always dials the /v1/listen path (deepgram.rs:479-480) and has no branch for /v2/listen; a search of gateway/src finds no speech-to-text client for that path. Today a session naming this model is accepted, because only the API key is checked, and is sent to /v1/listen. The resolver must refuse it before that client is built. The /v2/listen protocol is turn-based: the server reports start of turn, updates, an early end-of-turn guess, a resumed turn and end of turn. By default Deepgram decides the end of the turn from an end-of-turn threshold (0.7). Setting the threshold to 1.0 hands the decision to the client, which then sends a ForceEndTurn message when its own detector decides the turn is over; that is why the endpointing owner is recorded as selectable.

gateway_client.notes: No code takes one finished utterance and returns one transcript during a live session. The pieces to extract exist: a request builder for POST /v1/listen (batch.rs:346-353) and a response parser, today reached only from the two file-upload routes (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:223-225 and 607-610). The existing driver sends once, when the session disconnects, and then drops its callbacks (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); it uses a 300 s timeout and an HTTP/1.1 pool with a 90 s idle limit (prerecorded.rs:72, 177-185), and its parser marks every result as the end of the caller's turn (prerecorded.rs:897). None of that suits a live turn.

provenance.notes: Family row for a Deepgram id that starts with 'nova-' and has no exact row and does not start with 'nova-3-', for example a custom-trained Nova-2 model, or nova-2-phonecall and nova-2-atc, which are in Deepgram's documentation tables but in neither specification list. measurements.conditions: Pipecat's shipped constant DEEPGRAM_TTFS_P99 = 0.35 s (time from end of speech to final transcript, voice detector hangover 0.2 s). gateway_client.notes: No code takes one finished utterance and returns one transcript during a live session. billing.notes: Only the uploaded seconds are billed, per second with no minimum. Deepgram's pre-recorded prices differ from its streaming prices.

Deepgram quotes prices per minute and bills per second of audio with no minimum; its pricing page says a 14 second file is billed as exactly 14 seconds. This describes the first transport, the streaming socket, on which the gateway forwards every frame including silence; the evidence does not say in so many words that silence on a stream is billed, so bills_silence is left unknown. There is no entry for this model in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, and lookups there are exact (pricing.rs:466-469), so metering reports no price until one is added. The file transport carries its own billing block.

gateway_client.notes: Deepgram's Finalize message makes the server process buffered audio at once and return the final transcript. The client already recognises the from_finalize flag on a response (deepgram.rs:694-696) but nothing sends the message. Sending it when the gateway's own voice detector reports the end of speech would return the final without waiting for Deepgram's silence timer. This is an optional latency lever: Deepgram's own endpointing already ends utterances on this socket.

gateway_client.notes: No code takes one finished utterance and returns one transcript during a live session. The pieces to extract exist: a request builder for POST /v1/listen (batch.rs:346-353) and a response parser, today reached only from the two file-upload routes (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:223-225 and 607-610). The existing driver sends once, when the session disconnects, and then drops its callbacks (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); it uses a 300 s timeout and an HTTP/1.1 pool with a 90 s idle limit (prerecorded.rs:72, 177-185), and its parser marks every result as the end of the caller's turn (prerecorded.rs:897). None of that suits a live turn.

billing.notes: Only the uploaded seconds are billed, per second with no minimum. Deepgram's pre-recorded prices differ from its streaming prices.

Deepgram quotes prices per minute and bills per second of audio with no minimum; its pricing page says a 14 second file is billed as exactly 14 seconds. This describes the first transport, the streaming socket, on which the gateway forwards every frame including silence; the evidence does not say in so many words that silence on a stream is billed, so bills_silence is left unknown. There is no entry for this model in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, and lookups there are exact (pricing.rs:466-469), so metering reports no price until one is added. The file transport carries its own billing block.

gateway_client.notes: The client was exercised against Deepgram's live socket by key-gated tests that round-trip synthesised speech through it with nova-2 and nova-3 (gateway/tests/deepgram_live_e2e.rs:251-289), and Deepgram streaming was timed live for the gateway's latency analysis of 2026-06-05 (WaaV/LATENCY_ANALYSIS.md:18). The tests are marked ignore and continuous integration does not run them. This model id itself has not been exercised live; it uses the same client and differs only in the model query value. Each caller chunk is forwarded at once as one binary frame (deepgram.rs:950-957). Interim results are on. Deepgram decides where an utterance ends: the client asks for endpointing after 200 ms of silence by default (deepgram.rs:154, 520-523) and maps the vendor's speech_final flag to is_speech_final (deepgram.rs:684-690). segment_profile.rationale: One upload in flight per session instead of two, because Whisper Cloud allows as few as 3 concurrent requests for a whole Deepgram project; two per session would be exhausted by the second simultaneous call. The limit is per project, not per API key, so a shared cap across sessions is also needed and must be configurable per deployment. The 10 s request timeout is an engineering estimate from the vendor audit, not a vendor figure: no latency is published. Replace it with a deadline derived from measurement.

provenance.notes: Deepgram Whisper Cloud is file-only: the vendor states that live streaming is not available for it, and no whisper id is in the streaming specification's model list. The file endpoint POST /v1/listen is synchronous, so cutting the call into utterances and uploading each one is the only way to use this model on a live call. Today the gateway checks no model id and would send this id to the streaming socket (gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:486-491), where it cannot work; the error Deepgram returns was not observed. Capacity is small: 3 to 15 concurrent requests for a whole Deepgram project depending on which vendor page is read, so the model can carry only a handful of simultaneous calls. The host restriction is in constraints.regions. It supports neither keyterm nor keywords, nor entity detection, profanity filter or search. It returns no no-speech probability or average log probability, so a quality filter must use transcript and word confidence. Whisper was removed from Deepgram's self-hosted product on 2026-10-01; the hosted product is still documented and priced and has no retirement notice, so the status is ga. This id selects the medium size. The file transport is enabled from Release 3, default on (integration decisions, section 6); until then a live session naming this model is refused.

provenance.notes: Deepgram Whisper Cloud is file-only: the vendor states that live streaming is not available for it, and no whisper id is in the streaming specification's model list. The file endpoint POST /v1/listen is synchronous, so cutting the call into utterances and uploading each one is the only way to use this model on a live call. Today the gateway checks no model id and would send this id to the streaming socket (gateway/src/core/stt/deepgram.rs:486-491), where it cannot work; the error Deepgram returns was not observed. Capacity is small: 3 to 15 concurrent requests for a whole Deepgram project depending on which vendor page is read, so the model can carry only a handful of simultaneous calls. The host restriction is in constraints.regions. It supports neither keyterm nor keywords, nor entity detection, profanity filter or search. It returns no no-speech probability or average log probability, so a quality filter must use transcript and word confidence. Whisper was removed from Deepgram's self-hosted product on 2026-10-01; the hosted product is still documented and priced and has no retirement notice, so the status is ga. This is the size the bare id 'whisper' selects. The file transport is enabled from Release 3, default on (integration decisions, section 6); until then a live session naming this model is refused.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented. No per-utterance file adapter exists for live sessions, and this model has no streaming interface, so a live call cannot use it today.

regions.note: Whisper Cloud is offered on Deepgram's North America host only, not on the Europe, Australia or India hosts.

latency.notes: Deepgram publishes no latency for Whisper Cloud; it says only that its other models return results faster. Must be measured before this transport is enabled.

rates.note: Deepgram publishes 3, 5 and 15 on three pages without saying which plan each applies to; the lowest is recorded.

gateway_client.notes: No code takes one finished utterance and returns one transcript during a live session. The pieces to extract exist: a request builder for POST /v1/listen (batch.rs:346-353) and a response parser, today reached only from the two file-upload routes (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:223-225 and 607-610). The existing driver sends once, when the session disconnects, and then drops its callbacks (prerecorded.rs:1098-1112); it uses a 300 s timeout and an HTTP/1.1 pool with a 90 s idle limit (prerecorded.rs:72, 177-185), and its parser marks every result as the end of the caller's turn (prerecorded.rs:897). None of that suits a live turn. For Whisper Cloud the request builder also needs a per-model rule: it sends keyterm for every model (batch.rs:421-425), and Whisper Cloud supports neither keyterm nor keywords.

segment_profile.rationale: One upload in flight per session instead of two, because Whisper Cloud allows as few as 3 concurrent requests for a whole Deepgram project; two per session would be exhausted by the second simultaneous call. The limit is per project, not per API key, so a shared cap across sessions is also needed and must be configurable per deployment. The 10 s request timeout is an engineering estimate from the vendor audit, not a vendor figure: no latency is published. Replace it with a deadline derived from measurement.

transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls (segmented_elevenlabs) is not built yet. Today a live session that names this model fails at setup, and the existing upload driver sends audio only at disconnect.

rates.note: Every HTTP request counts. Over the limit the vendor queues the request (about 50 ms) or answers 429 concurrent_limit_exceeded; the maximum-concurrent-requests response header carries the account's real ceiling.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request builder and the response parser already serve the upload route, but the driver's flush takes &mut self and runs only at disconnect, on a shared HTTP client with a 300 s timeout that is limited to HTTP/1.1 (prerecorded.rs:72, :177-185), so two uploads cannot be in flight. A live session that names a file model fails session setup with a named error (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/config.rs:391). The live request must differ from the upload route: send tag_audio_events=false (the vendor default is true and writes tokens such as (laughter) into the text; the parser removes them from the word list but not from the text, prerecorded.rs:1003-1008); send language_code when the language is known; keep timestamps_granularity=word, because per-word log-probability is the only quality signal; send at most 100 key terms and never transcript_edit. The parser hard-codes confidence 1.0 and drops language_probability and transcription_id (prerecorded.rs:1033-1048). The upload route overwrites the configured region with the driver's base URL (gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:776). The vendor says raw 16 kHz PCM with file_format=pcm_s16le_16 is faster than an encoded file; the builder always sends file_format=other (elevenlabs/batch.rs:488-500) and the switch waits for one live probe. For an unknown id the adapter sends no key terms (they carry a surcharge and their support per model is unknown) and reads no quality fields.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. The upload route's shared client allows 300 s (gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:72); the vendor audit proposes 8 s in total and 2 s to connect, about four times the only measured P99 (2.01 s). This is an inference, not a measurement, and must be replaced once the gateway has its own numbers; how processing time grows with segment length is unknown. The container stays 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV with file_format=other until a live probe confirms the vendor's faster raw PCM option. Pre-roll, trailing silence, the 25 s maximum segment and two uploads in flight keep the defaults; the vendor's own limits (10 hours, 5 GB) never bind.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised against the vendor once: the key-gated live test elevenlabs_stt_transcribes_live drove this client through create_stt_standard with scribe_v2_realtime and got the spoken sentence back on 2026-06-04 (commit 7acd6c9, whose message records the run). That date is the last known good, not a current check. The status follows the rule the fact-check applied to the Sarvam client, which was verified by the same test file in the same commit. Since that run the WebSocket upgrade request is built by into_client_request instead of by hand, an endpoint override and a model check were added, and the shutdown signal changed (client.rs, 2026-07-12, commit 151cd1c; config.rs, up to 2026-09-25, commit 73a378a); the query parameters and the audio frame are the same (read from the diff between 7acd6c9 and the current head; messages.rs has not changed since 2026-01-18). The live test is ignored by default, is not part of CI and was not re-run, and the 2026-10-03 vendor audit made no live call, so re-run it with a working key before relying on this status. The client is also covered by unit tests of the socket URL and message parsing (gateway/src/core/stt/elevenlabs/tests.rs, run by CI) and by a mock-socket test (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1367, not one of the test binaries CI runs). The audit found three departures from the vendor's published protocol; none is known to stop transcription: each audio chunk omits the commit and sample_rate fields that the vendor schema marks as required (messages.rs:32-39; the same omission was present in the 2026-06-04 run, which passed); the message parser recognises three of the vendor's error types (messages.rs:386) and treats the rest as unknown; and the URL builder sends no key terms, diarization, entity detection or no_verbatim. A fourth departure matters only when word timestamps are requested: the vendor then pairs every commit with a second message, committed_transcript_with_timestamps (stated in a comment in Pipecat's client, which skips the first message for that reason; read from the source file the audit fetched, not covered by the fact-check), and the gateway maps both messages to a final result that ends the turn (client.rs:488-510), so one utterance probably ends the turn twice (inferred from reading, not run). The client always asks the vendor to commit by voice-activity detection after 0.5 s of silence (config.rs:337-340; client.rs:400-431) and maps each committed transcript to a final result that also ends the turn (client.rs:488-499). It reports confidence 1.0 for a committed transcript, or a value derived from per-word log-probabilities when word timestamps were requested (client.rs:501-510). The socket accepts PCM at 8 to 48 kHz and 8 kHz mu-law. The vendor starts transcribing after the first 2 seconds of audio and closes a socket after 15 s without client messages.

segment_profile.rationale: Provisional and inferred, not a vendor fact. The 25 s default exists for Whisper's 30 s window, which does not apply here; the vendor documents no maximum and describes the engine as built for basic command sentences, and a synchronous decode takes longer as audio gets longer. Split at the last pause before 15 s and raise it only after a probe with a real key shows longer segments are accepted and accurate. Uploads in flight stay at the default of two; drop to one for the session after any status 9 (system busy), the vendor's only back-pressure signal. The 8 s request timeout is the audit's conversational budget, not a measurement: the vendor publishes no response time, and the client's own 60 s (config.rs:26) is useless for a turn. gateway_client.notes: The gateway has no file code for Gladia: it is absent from both lists of file-upload vendors (batch.rs:839-844; prerecorded.rs:102-123). The vendor's file API is an asynchronous job in three steps: upload the audio (POST /v2/upload, multipart field audio), create the job (POST /v2/pre-recorded with the returned audio address and the model), then poll (GET /v2/pre-recorded/{id}) until the status is done or error. Every call carries the x-gladia-key header. There is no synchronous endpoint that can select a model. The closest existing template is the AssemblyAI upload-and-poll driver, whose timing (first poll at 500 ms, backing off to 3 s, 300 s deadline, prerecorded.rs:72-94) suits whole files, not a live turn. Vendor rules an adapter must follow: never create a second job for the same audio once a job id has been returned, because each accepted job is billed and nothing is deduplicated; retry the upload or the create call only on a transport failure, a server error or a rate-limit response received before a job id exists; a failed poll may be retried. Uploaded audio and transcripts are kept three weeks on paid plans and a year on the free plan unless the job is deleted, and accounts with zero data retention cannot use the upload or the polling call at all.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock (a mock end-to-end test) and unit tests; the evidence records no run against Gladia. Connecting takes two steps: a POST to /v2/live with the X-Gladia-Key header returns a socket address for the session (client.rs:101-107), which the client then dials. Each caller chunk is forwarded at once, as a base64 JSON text frame through a 32-slot channel (client.rs:216-229, 502). Partial transcripts are requested by default (config.rs:273-287). Gladia decides where the utterance ends: the request asks for a cut after 50 ms of silence and a forced cut after 5 s without a pause (mod.rs:76-79; client.rs:75-76), and Gladia's final flag is copied into both is_final and is_speech_final (client.rs:249-254), so every vendor final ends the caller's turn. Gladia's own guidance for voice agents is a forced cut at 15 s. The model sent is always solaria-1, whatever the session asked for (config.rs:493, 541-551; client.rs:74). The request body has drifted from Gladia's current schema in three places. A word-timestamp field the schema does not have (words_accurate_timestamps) is written into every request, whether or not the session asked for word times, because the field has no rule to leave it out (config.rs:345-346; client.rs:79). A translation-target field the schema does not have, and custom vocabulary sent as a list where the schema has a boolean plus a separate list, are written only when the session asks for translation or key terms (config.rs:348-349, 364-365). Whether Gladia rejects or ignores a field it does not know is unknown, so every Gladia session today depends on Gladia ignoring the first one. A reconnect opens a new session (client.rs:557-560), although Gladia says reconnecting to the same address resumes the old one.

gateway_client.notes: The gateway has no file code for Gladia: it is absent from both lists of file-upload vendors (batch.rs:839-844; prerecorded.rs:102-123). The vendor's file API is an asynchronous job in three steps: upload the audio (POST /v2/upload, multipart field audio), create the job (POST /v2/pre-recorded with the returned audio address and the model), then poll (GET /v2/pre-recorded/{id}) until the status is done or error. Every call carries the x-gladia-key header. There is no synchronous endpoint that can select a model. The closest existing template is the AssemblyAI upload-and-poll driver, whose timing (first poll at 500 ms, backing off to 3 s, 300 s deadline, prerecorded.rs:72-94) suits whole files, not a live turn. Vendor rules an adapter must follow: never create a second job for the same audio once a job id has been returned, because each accepted job is billed and nothing is deduplicated; retry the upload or the create call only on a transport failure, a server error or a rate-limit response received before a job id exists; a failed poll may be retried. Uploaded audio and transcripts are kept three weeks on paid plans and a year on the free plan unless the job is deleted, and accounts with zero data retention cannot use the upload or the polling call at all.

segment_profile.rationale: The 10 s deadline covers the whole upload, create and poll cycle and is an engineering estimate from the vendor audit; nothing is published. The audit suggests about 5 s per HTTP call and a first poll about 200 ms after the job is created, backing off to 1 s; the schema has no field for poll timing. Two uploads in flight per session is unchanged, but jobs count against a limit for the whole account (3 on the free plan, 25 running plus 300 queued on paid plans), so a limiter shared across sessions is needed. Every other setting keeps the gateway default: Gladia converts everything to 16 kHz WAV and lists no conversion cost for WAV, mono avoids per-channel billing, and no minimum billed duration is documented, so short segments are not merged.

gateway_client.defect: The existing gRPC client calls the method path /Listener/DoSpeechToText, while the vendor's published client stub calls /SpeechToText.Listener/DoSpeechToText, so the vendor server is expected to reject the call as unimplemented. This was read from the vendor's stub and was not tested against the live service. The service itself is absent from the vendor's current documentation. The id 'default' selects the older asr.gnani.ai gRPC service. The gateway's client for it calls a method path the vendor's own stub does not define, and that service has no file endpoint open to ordinary customers. Use gnani-prisma-v2.5, which will be served by file upload once that adapter exists.
gateway_client.notes: This is the client every Gnani session gets today, whatever model is named, because the client never validates or sends the model. It dials https://asr.gnani.ai:443 and authenticates with a token, an access key and a certificate. The token and the access key can come from process environment variables or from per-session provider settings (config.rs:133-138, 159-160); the certificate can only come from process environment variables (config.rs:161-164), and a token set only in the server's configuration file is not used, because the client ignores the api_key field in which the server delivers it (gateway/src/config/mod.rs:672-677). Further defects found by reading the code: a final result whose text equals the previous interim result is dropped, so turn-taking never sees the end of that utterance (client.rs:400-415); connect() reports success before any stream is opened (client.rs:73-81); and the language list is the legacy one, which rejects the vendor's current Punjabi code pa-IN (config.rs:359-381). When the transport is stuck, audio ingest for the session blocks once two chained queues of 100 frames each are full, about 4 s of 20 ms frames, or about 2 s between reconnect attempts when only one queue exists (client.rs:99, 305, 539). The only test is a mock server that registers the same short service name, so it cannot catch the path mismatch.

gateway_client.defect: Google closes the stream on this model after every utterance, and the gateway's Google client has no single-utterance handling. It treats each close as a dropped stream, records a failure on the circuit breaker that every Google session shares, and reconnects after a delay that grows with each attempt. The retry budget is ten attempts and is cleared only when a stream has stayed open for 30 seconds, so a call whose caller speaks more often than that loses transcription after about ten utterances. Three closes in a row within 5 seconds of their connect put the shared breaker in its fatal state for 60 seconds, which also stops other Google sessions from connecting. All of this is read in the code and was never run against Google. Until the client treats the per-utterance close as normal, a model that keeps the stream open (long, latest_long, telephony) is the better choice.
