transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls (segmented_openai_compat) is not built yet. Today the Groq client buffers the caller audio and uploads it only at hang-up, when the client ends its audio by hand (audio_end, or a commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), or when its 20 MB buffer cap is reached, so a normal call gets no transcript while it is in progress.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request code lives inside the buffering client: send_request takes &mut self and writes rate-limit state and the last request id, so two uploads cannot be in flight; it is awaited on the audio path under the voice manager's speech-to-text write lock (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:636-639) behind a 120 s request timeout, a 30 s connect timeout and a three-attempt loop (client.rs:57, :60, :66). The loop retries network errors and timeouts; a typed 429 or 5xx reply is probably returned on the first attempt, because the retry test looks for the status digits or a lower-case 'rate limit' in a message that holds neither unless the vendor's error body failed to parse (client.rs:640-653, :806-825; inferred from reading, not run). The worst stall on the audio path is therefore three 120 s timeouts plus back-off, and a rate-limit reply probably fails the upload at once instead of waiting. The WAV is written at the session sample rate and channel count (client.rs:520-522), not 16 kHz mono. Groq speaks the OpenAI multipart request, so the shared OpenAI-compatible transcriber serves it with base URL https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 (config.rs:35). For an unknown id the adapter asks for the plain json format and reads no quality fields, because verbose_json segment fields are only established for the Whisper models. Take the language hint from the provider-mapped value: on the /ws path the configured language is mapped to ISO 639-1, with `auto` omitted, before the client is built (gateway/src/handlers/ws/config.rs:475-504; gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:239-242), while the DAG node passes its own default en-US unmapped (gateway/src/dag/nodes/provider.rs:334-343).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. The existing client allows 120 s per request, 30 s to connect and up to three attempts on network errors and timeouts (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/client.rs:57, :60, :66); the vendor audit recommends 5 s in total with one retry at most, roughly three times the third-party P99 of 1.54 s. It is an estimate to be replaced by the gateway's own measurement. Container (16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV: Groq downsamples to 16 kHz mono and says WAV gives lower latency), pre-roll, trailing silence, the 25 s maximum segment and two uploads in flight keep the defaults. Segments are still uploaded at each pause: the 10 s minimum billed per request costs about $0.0001 (turbo) or $0.0003 (large-v3), too little to justify holding a segment back. The binding constraint is the per-organisation request limit, so a deployment on the free plan (20 requests per minute) may choose upload_policy per_turn.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. The existing client allows 120 s per request, 30 s to connect and up to three attempts on network errors and timeouts (gateway/src/core/stt/groq/client.rs:57, :60, :66); the vendor audit recommends 5 s in total with one retry at most, roughly three times the third-party P99 of 1.54 s. It is an estimate to be replaced by the gateway's own measurement. Container (16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV: Groq downsamples to 16 kHz mono and says WAV gives lower latency), pre-roll, trailing silence, the 25 s maximum segment and two uploads in flight keep the defaults. measurements.conditions: Pipecat constant GROQ_TTFS_P99 = 1.54 s: end of speech to final transcript for its voice-activity-segmented Groq service, including a 200 ms detector stop delay. gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1245-1267); the evidence records no live call to IBM. Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). For an id the map does not know, the client passes the string to IBM unchanged (config.rs:597-599). IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST {instance URL}/v1/recognize with the WAV file as the raw request body (Content-Type audio/wav; not multipart) and the model and options in the query string. Send a cached IAM bearer token: IBM says passing the API key directly 'might affect performance', and a token lasts up to 60 minutes. Do not copy the streaming client's audio/l16 content type: IBM warns that its endianness detection can drop the connection on short audio. A request needs at least 100 bytes. One response can hold several results, one for each pause longer than 0.8 seconds, and the adapter must join their transcripts. Asking for audio_metrics=true returns speech_ratio, the closest thing IBM has to a no-speech signal; the map's signal list has no name for it. The 100 concurrent requests of the Plus plan are counted across WebSocket and HTTP together, so a session that falls back to upload must close its socket first and the engine needs a limiter for the whole IBM service instance. The audit's 10 second request timeout is a placeholder with no vendor basis and is not recorded. IBM's asynchronous job API (POST /v1/recognitions, then poll) is not a live transport and is not listed.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. IBM's socket accepts many recognition requests on one connection: binary audio, then {"action":"stop"}, then the final results, then {"state":"listening"}, after which the next request needs no new start message. The gateway would keep streaming audio as it arrives and send stop when its own detector reports end of speech, so IBM finalises at once instead of waiting out its 0.8 second pause. Interim results keep arriving while the caller speaks, there is no upload, and the session uses one of the instance's concurrency slots. The latency gain is inferred from the documentation and has not been measured. It is a change to the existing client, not to the shared file-upload adapter.

billing.notes: Priced per minute of audio sent. IBM does not round up each call: usage is summed over the month and rounded to the nearest minute at month end, so there is no per-request minimum. Silence is billed like speech, so an open socket bills the whole call. The per-minute price was confirmed only in a pricing page dated 2024-04-19. No pricing_key: gateway/src/config/pricing.rs has speech-to-text entries only for en-US_Multimedia and en-US_Telephony.

provenance.notes: Default for an IBM model id the map has never seen, for example a new locale or a customer's custom model. The existing streaming client is listed first, as the conversion rule for a working native client requires, so such a session gets what it gets today, with interim results. IBM states that every interface offers the same transcription for every model, so an unknown but valid id streams. The client is not sound: it very probably stops transcribing after 30 seconds of caller silence, and it sends two start-message keys that IBM documents as unavailable for large speech models. The first is recorded in this row's gateway_client.defect; the second matters only for a large speech model id and is recorded on those rows. IBM's synchronous file endpoint, which serves every model family, is listed behind it as a fallback, but no release builds an IBM file transcriber, so that transport is never enabled. The resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. Four ids that the gateway itself produces as language defaults are not IBM models and land on this row: es-LA_Multimedia, zh-CN_Multimedia, ar-MS_Multimedia and hi-IN_Multimedia (gateway/src/core/stt/ibm_watson/config.rs:605, 613, 615, 616). They have no row because the map has no way to mark an id as known to be invalid; the code must remap them to the matching _Telephony or large speech id.

provenance.notes: A glob row, because the discontinued family has one id for each locale and the evidence does not list them all. The replacement entries are patterns, not literal ids, in order of preference: the same locale with the _Multimedia suffix, then the _Telephony suffix for the locales that have no multimedia model, as IBM's own table of discontinued models does (read in the copy of models.md that the audit fetched; the audit and the fact-check quote only the discontinuation sentence from that page). IBM notes that the service downsamples audio to the model's rate, so broadband audio sent to a telephony model still works. The five regional Spanish broadband ids map to es-LA_Telephony, so neither pattern resolves for them. A check that every replacement names a row that is not retired has to treat these entries as patterns. The gateway passes these ids to IBM unchanged today (gateway/src/core/stt/ibm_watson/config.rs:597-599), and gateway/src/config/pricing.rs still has entries for en-US_NarrowbandModel and en-US_BroadbandModel. Earlier refusal wording (engineering note, replaced 2026-10-04 by customer text): Previous-generation IBM broadband models were discontinued on 1 August 2023; IBM says new clients must use the next-generation models. Refuse the session at setup and name the replacement. IBM's own table of discontinued models gives the multimedia model of the same locale (for example en-US_Multimedia for en-US_BroadbandModel). Where no multimedia model exists it gives a telephony model instead: ar-MS_Telephony, zh-CN_Telephony, and es-LA_Telephony for the five regional Spanish ids es-AR, es-CL, es-CO, es-MX and es-PE. Where a large speech model exists for the locale (its id is the bare locale, for example en-US), IBM's migration page calls that the optimal target.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1245-1267); the evidence records no live call to IBM. Each inbound frame is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:177-195). Interim results are on by default. IBM marks a result final after its own pause, 0.8 s by default (0.6 s for Chinese); the gateway cannot change that pause through the standard configuration. The client never sends stop during a call, and is_speech_final is in practice never true: it needs the end_of_utterance field, which IBM returns only when split_transcript_at_phrase_end is true, and the client always sends false (messages.rs:113-117, config.rs:750). So the gateway's own turn logic decides the end of the turn and IBM supplies only is_final. Defects found by reading, none reproduced live: the client asks for a 30 second no-speech timeout (config.rs:45, 749); when it fires IBM sends 'No speech detected for 30s' and closes, the client's lower-case error match misses that message (messages.rs:245-258), and a Close frame is treated as an intended end (client.rs:686-689, 207-213), so speech-to-text stops for the rest of the call whenever the caller is silent for 30 seconds. The region is always us-south (config.rs:635). The instance id is read only from provider extras on the standard path (config.rs:508-514); the registry path builds the client with an empty instance id and cannot connect (client.rs:949, 716-720). The access token is placed in the URL once and reused on every reconnect although tokens last at most 60 minutes (client.rs:729). Audio is declared as audio/l16 without endianness (config.rs:294). Word timings, word confidence and speaker labels are requested but not copied into the result, and a missing confidence becomes 0.0 (messages.rs:108-121). This model family needs audio sampled at 16 kHz or higher. The design frame records that the speech-to-text leg receives audio at the rate the caller sent it (not re-read for this row), so an 8 kHz telephone leg is below the model's minimum on this transport. IBM accepts at most 100 MB of audio in one recognition request on the socket. The client opens one request when it connects (client.rs:126-136) and sends stop only at shutdown (client.rs:113-122), so a call reaches that limit after about 52 minutes of 16 kHz audio (about 35 minutes at 24 kHz, 104 minutes at 8 kHz). What IBM does at the limit was not observed; this is inferred from the vendor page and the code.

Found by reading, not reproduced live.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. IBM's socket accepts many recognition requests on one connection: binary audio, then {"action":"stop"}, then the final results, then {"state":"listening"}, after which the next request needs no new start message. The gateway would keep streaming audio as it arrives and send stop when its own detector reports end of speech, so IBM finalises at once instead of waiting out its 0.8 second pause. Interim results keep arriving while the caller speaks, there is no upload, and the session uses one of the instance's concurrency slots. The latency gain is inferred from the documentation and has not been measured. It is a change to the existing client, not to the shared file-upload adapter.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented. No IBM file-request code exists in the gateway (gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:839-844 and gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:102-123 do not include IBM). Fallback only: IBM says the synchronous HTTP method is 'appropriate for batch processing but not for live speech recognition', and it returns no interim results.

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST {instance URL}/v1/recognize with the WAV file as the raw request body (Content-Type audio/wav; not multipart) and the model and options in the query string. Send a cached IAM bearer token: IBM says passing the API key directly 'might affect performance', and a token lasts up to 60 minutes. Do not copy the streaming client's audio/l16 content type: IBM warns that its endianness detection can drop the connection on short audio. A request needs at least 100 bytes. One response can hold several results, one for each pause longer than 0.8 seconds, and the adapter must join their transcripts. Asking for audio_metrics=true returns speech_ratio, the closest thing IBM has to a no-speech signal; the map's signal list has no name for it. The 100 concurrent requests of the Plus plan are counted across WebSocket and HTTP together, so a session that falls back to upload must close its socket first and the engine needs a limiter for the whole IBM service instance. The audit's 10 second request timeout is a placeholder with no vendor basis and is not recorded. IBM's asynchronous job API (POST /v1/recognitions, then poll) is not a live transport and is not listed. The gateway's default 16 kHz upload meets this family's 16 kHz minimum.

billing.notes: Only uploaded segments are billed, their padding included. IBM sums usage over the month and rounds at month end, so there is no per-request minimum.

Priced per minute of audio sent. IBM does not round up each call: usage is summed over the month and rounded to the nearest minute at month end, so there is no per-request minimum. Silence is billed like speech, so an open socket bills the whole call. The per-minute price was confirmed only in a pricing page dated 2024-04-19.

IBM documents the first as not available with large speech models and the second for en-US only among them, and says a request that includes an unsupported low_latency fails with status 400. Whether an explicit false is rejected has never been tested; the in-repo mock does not check it. Audio is forwarded frame by frame with interim results on. IBM finalises a result after its own 0.8 s pause (0.6 s for Chinese) and, as configured, never signals end of speech, so the gateway's turn logic ends the turn. Main risk, read but not reproduced: after 30 s without speech IBM closes the session and the client does not reconnect (config.rs:749; client.rs:686-689). Only the standard construction path connects, and only to us-south. Full description: the en-US_Multimedia row and the provider notes.
gateway_client.defect: Very probably stops transcribing for the rest of the call after 30 seconds of caller silence: the client asks IBM for a 30 second no-speech timeout, misses IBM's capitalised timeout message and treats the Close frame that follows as an intended end (config.rs:45, 749; messages.rs:245-258; client.rs:207-213, 686-689). Found by reading, not reproduced live. Its start message also always carries split_transcript_at_phrase_end=false and low_latency=false (config.rs:750-751), which IBM documents as unavailable on large speech models (low_latency is available on en-US only); whether an explicit false returns 400 is untested.

provenance.notes: IBM large speech model; the model id is the locale and fixes the language. Served on the WebSocket interface with interim results (since 2025-11-25) and on synchronous HTTP, so it is not file-only and file upload is a fallback. Accepts 8 kHz and 16 kHz audio. It has no low_latency mode. No keywords, no grammar_name and no split_transcript_at_phrase_end; parameter_set=enhanced is supported (since 2026-06-29).

rates.note: Plus plan, per service instance, counted across WebSocket and HTTP together. Premium plans have no concurrency limit; the Lite plan's limit is not published.

context_params.note: The id of a custom language model built on this base model; IBM's only vocabulary mechanism. Today's client sends it when configured (config.rs:720).

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock; the evidence records no live call to IBM. Audio is forwarded frame by frame with interim results on. IBM finalises a result after its own 0.8 s pause (0.6 s for Chinese) and, as configured, never signals end of speech, so the gateway's turn logic ends the turn. Main risk, read but not reproduced: after 30 s without speech IBM closes the session and the client does not reconnect (config.rs:749; client.rs:686-689). Only the standard construction path connects, and only to us-south. Full description: the en-US_Multimedia row and the provider notes. Needs 16 kHz audio or higher; an 8 kHz telephone leg forwarded at its own rate is below that minimum.
gateway_client.defect: Very probably stops transcribing for the rest of the call after 30 seconds of caller silence: the client asks IBM for a 30 second no-speech timeout, misses IBM's capitalised timeout message and treats the Close frame that follows as an intended end (config.rs:45, 749; messages.rs:245-258; client.rs:207-213, 686-689). Found by reading, not reproduced live.

gateway_client.notes: CLOVA Speech Recognition (CSR): POST https://naveropenapi.apigw.ntruss.com/recog/v1/stt?lang=<Kor|Eng|Jpn|Chn>, raw file body, text-only response. transcribe_buffer already builds this request and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: always wrap PCM in a WAV container and always send Content-Type application/octet-stream (the vendor rejects any other content type and lists no raw PCM format; today the client sends headerless PCM by default and audio/wav or audio/mpeg otherwise, client.rs:136-140, config.rs:147-153); resample to 16 kHz, the vendor minimum (the constructor rejects lower session rates, config.rs:369-374); keep uploads longer than 400 ms (min_audio_ms is an exclusive bound), under 60 s and under 3 MB; treat the vendor's HTTP 500 for unreadable audio as a request fault so one bad upload does not open the breaker shared by all sessions; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 1.0 (client.rs:349). The quota in limits.rates is per console application and adjustable; HTTP 429 means it is used up. The legacy client reports every HTTP 413 as 'Audio too long (max 60 seconds)' (client.rs:197-199), although the vendor answers 413 both for audio over 60 s and for a body over 3 MB; the adapter should tell the two apart by the vendor's error code.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 10000 ms is the vendor audit's starting value, not a measurement: no latency is published for any NAVER file API, and the legacy client allows 30 s (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/client.rs:54-58). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB as 16 kHz WAV, inside 60 s and 3 MB, and the default padding keeps every upload above the 400 ms minimum. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause). Calls that arrive at 8 kHz must be upsampled to 16 kHz before upload.

gateway_client.notes: POST {InvokeURL}/recognizer/upload, multipart form with the file and a JSON parameter block, header X-CLOVASPEECH-API-KEY. The vendor's default is an asynchronous job; setting completion=sync makes the same request block and return the result, which is the mode a live call must use and the mode LiveKit's Clova plugin uses. It is the only NAVER file API that returns confidence (overall and per segment, 0 to 1) and word times. For short segments switch off the defaults that add work: speaker diarization, noise filtering and word alignment are all on by default. Languages ko-KR, en-US, enko (mixed), ja, zh-cn, zh-tw. gateway_client.notes: CLOVA Speech Recognition (CSR): POST https://naveropenapi.apigw.ntruss.com/recog/v1/stt?lang=<Kor|Eng|Jpn|Chn>, raw file body, text-only response. transcribe_buffer already builds this request and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: always wrap PCM in a WAV container and always send Content-Type application/octet-stream (the vendor rejects any other content type and lists no raw PCM format; today the client sends headerless PCM by default and audio/wav or audio/mpeg otherwise, client.rs:136-140, config.rs:147-153); resample to 16 kHz, the vendor minimum (the constructor rejects lower session rates, config.rs:369-374); keep uploads longer than 400 ms (min_audio_ms is an exclusive bound), under 60 s and under 3 MB; treat the vendor's HTTP 500 for unreadable audio as a request fault so one bad upload does not open the breaker shared by all sessions; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 1.0 (client.rs:349). The quota in limits.rates is per console application and adjustable; HTTP 429 means it is used up. The legacy client reports every HTTP 413 as 'Audio too long (max 60 seconds)' (client.rs:197-199), although the vendor answers 413 both for audio over 60 s and for a body over 3 MB; the adapter should tell the two apart by the vendor's error code.

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 10000 ms is the vendor audit's starting value, not a measurement: no latency is published for any NAVER file API, and the legacy client allows 30 s (gateway/src/core/stt/naver_clova/client.rs:54-58). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB as 16 kHz WAV, inside 60 s and 3 MB, and the default padding keeps every upload above the 400 ms minimum. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause). Calls that arrive at 8 kHz must be upsampled to 16 kHz before upload.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request and response code lives inside the buffering client: flush_buffer wraps the whole buffered call in one WAV at the session sample rate, is awaited on the audio path under the voice manager's speech-to-text write lock (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:636-639) and uses a 30 s timeout (client.rs:54). Field mapping must change for this model: the client sends the singular `language` field for every model (config.rs:856-858) and folds key terms into `prompt` (config.rs:773-777), while the vendor documents `languages[]` and `keywords[]` here and says not to send both language fields. transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls does not exist yet. The gateway has no gRPC client for Phonexia Speech Platform 4. Before it can be enabled for a model id the map has not seen, a deployment must also declare which model its gRPC endpoint runs: the request has no model field and the Whisper model is fixed when the microservice starts, so a named model would otherwise be ignored without any error. Only the REST interface can select a model for each request. The plan builds this transport only when a customer needs it, because Phonexia runs on the customer's premises.

latency.notes: Not measured. The vendor publishes throughput only (for example about 17 times faster than real time for English Whisper on one named GPU with 100 s files) and no latency for short audio. It depends on the customer's hardware and must be measured per deployment.

rates.note: The Whisper microservice's default of one instance per device. A deployment that runs more instances should raise it through its override.

gateway_client.notes: No code exists for this transport. The call (Transcribe, default port 8080) is synchronous: the audio is uploaded in messages of at most 4 MiB, the client closes its side, and the transcript comes back on the same call. The vendor states that transcription starts only after the whole audio has been received, so this is a file upload and not a live stream. A 25 s segment at 16 kHz is about 800 kB and fits in one message. Audio must be mono. The gateway already has hand-written gRPC clients without code generation that can serve as a pattern (tinkoff/grpc.rs:230). Overload is answered with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and an expired licence with FAILED_PRECONDITION. No authentication is documented. For this engine the request has no model field: the Whisper model is fixed when the microservice starts, so a model name in the session can only be honoured if the deployment declares that its endpoint runs that model. The language is optional and defaults to automatic detection, which the vendor bases on the first 30 s of audio; a live call should pin the language because short segments give detection little to work with. Each segment of the response carries the detected source language. There is no prompt or vocabulary field. The vendor states that this engine needs a GPU.

segment_profile.rationale: By default the vendor's software processes one request per engine at a time: on the Virtual Appliance each technology has one replica, and the Whisper microservice starts with one instance per device. A second upload in flight would be rejected with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on gRPC or would queue on REST, so it only moves the wait. A deployment that runs more instances should raise this through its override.

transports.disabled_reason: The file-upload adapter for live calls does not exist yet, and this interface is an asynchronous task: the upload is answered with HTTP 202 and a Location header, and the result must be polled. Nothing in the evidence shows that it answers within about two seconds.

latency.notes: Not measured. The task is queued, the media file is converted, and the result is polled; none of these steps has a published duration.

rates.note: The Virtual Appliance's default of one replica per technology: one request is processed at a time and further requests are queued. A deployment may run more.

gateway_client.notes: No code exists for this transport. The request is multipart form data with the field file, sent to the Virtual Appliance (port 8000 in the vendor's examples). The reply is 202 with a Location header; the gateway then polls the task until it is done, failed, rejected or cancelled, and should cancel it with DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id} when the caller interrupts or hangs up. The gateway's existing polling helper starts at 500 ms and backs off to 3 s (prerecorded.rs:82-94), which is too coarse for one turn of a conversation; the audit suggests a fixed 100 to 200 ms, which is its own estimate. The limits recorded are the vendor's configurable defaults: uploads up to 500 MB, audio up to 2 hours, processing cancelled after 5 minutes, one request at a time per technology, extra requests queued. Any media file is accepted and converted first; MP3 and MP4 are the examples the vendor names. The response has no confidence value. No authentication is documented. For this engine the path is /api/technology/speech-to-text-whisper-enhanced. The optional model query parameter selects an installed Whisper model and defaults to 'default'; a model that is not deployed is answered with 404 model.not-deployed and a list of available models. The language is optional and defaults to automatic detection; each segment of the result carries the detected language.

gateway_client.notes: This is the client every Phonexia session gets today, and it fails at session setup. With a public server address it fails in connect() with a configuration error (client.rs:276-290); with a private address, which is the normal case for an on-premises server, it fails earlier because the server address is rejected by the check against private networks (config.rs:282-287). The client reads the session's model field as a result type and its api_key field as the server address (config.rs:407-430), so no real model can be selected. The only final result it recognises is the vendor's is_last flag, which marks the end of the whole stream, so even a connected session would never end a turn (client.rs:138-154). The module's own header says the protocol is unverified (mod.rs:12-20).

gateway_client.notes: No code exists for this transport. The request is multipart form data with the field file, sent to the Virtual Appliance (port 8000 in the vendor's examples). The reply is 202 with a Location header; the gateway then polls the task until it is done, failed, rejected or cancelled, and should cancel it with DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id} when the caller interrupts or hangs up. The gateway's existing polling helper starts at 500 ms and backs off to 3 s (prerecorded.rs:82-94), which is too coarse for one turn of a conversation; the audit suggests a fixed 100 to 200 ms, which is its own estimate. The limits recorded are the vendor's configurable defaults: uploads up to 500 MB, audio up to 2 hours, processing cancelled after 5 minutes, one request at a time per technology, extra requests queued. Any media file is accepted and converted first; MP3 and MP4 are the examples the vendor names. The response has no confidence value. No authentication is documented. For this engine the path is /api/technology/speech-to-text, the language query parameter is required and selects the language model, and there is no model parameter. Whether a region tag such as en-US is accepted, or only the deployed names such as en, is not confirmed. Vocabulary is biased through preferred_phrases and additional_words in the config form field. On the Virtual Appliance instances of this engine are started on demand by default, which adds a cold start; a live deployment must make them permanent. The transcript contains literal <silence/> tokens.

segment_profile.rationale: On the Virtual Appliance each technology has one replica by default, so one request is processed at a time. For the stand-alone microservice of this engine the vendor's help text prints no default for the number of concurrent requests; one is assumed until a deployment says otherwise. A second upload in flight would be rejected with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED on gRPC or would queue on REST, so it only moves the wait. A deployment that runs more instances should raise this through its override.

latency.notes: Not measured. The vendor publishes throughput only (for example about 17 times faster than real time for English Whisper on one named GPU with 100 s files) and no latency for short audio. It depends on the customer's hardware and must be measured per deployment.

gateway_client.notes: No code exists for this transport. The call (Transcribe, default port 8080) is synchronous: the audio is uploaded in messages of at most 4 MiB, the client closes its side, and the transcript comes back on the same call. The vendor states that transcription starts only after the whole audio has been received, so this is a file upload and not a live stream. A 25 s segment at 16 kHz is about 800 kB and fits in one message. Audio must be mono. The gateway already has hand-written gRPC clients without code generation that can serve as a pattern (tinkoff/grpc.rs:230). Overload is answered with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and an expired licence with FAILED_PRECONDITION. No authentication is documented. For this engine the request has no model field: the Whisper model is fixed when the microservice starts, so a model name in the session can only be honoured if the deployment declares that its endpoint runs that model. The language is optional and defaults to automatic detection, which the vendor bases on the first 30 s of audio; a live call should pin the language because short segments give detection little to work with. Each segment of the response carries the detected source language. There is no prompt or vocabulary field. The vendor states that this engine needs a GPU.

gateway_client.notes: Never exercised against Rev AI: the only end-to-end test runs against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:9 says the gateway holds no Rev AI key). One long-lived socket per call; each caller chunk is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:111-116). Vendor 'partial' becomes an interim result and vendor 'final' becomes is_final and is_speech_final (client.rs:327-348). Defects found by reading, none of which stop transcription: partial text is joined with no separator, so interim text reads 'onetooth' (messages.rs:188-190); connect() returns on the HTTP upgrade, not on the vendor 'connected' frame, although the vendor requires waiting for it (client.rs:90-97, 323-326); every vendor final is flagged end of speech although Rev AI finals are commit points, not end-of-utterance markers (client.rs:348); a server Close frame with a standard code such as 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1013 ends the session instead of reconnecting (messages.rs:34-45, 62-64; client.rs:142-157); chunks are not aggregated to the 250 ms the vendor asks for (mod.rs:100 is unused). For an id the gateway does not recognise it omits the transcriber query parameter, so the account's default streaming model answers (config.rs:541-553; the test at config.rs:759-766 pins that an unknown id does not error).
gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, none of which stops transcription: interim text is joined without spaces, every vendor final is flagged end of speech although Rev AI finals are commit points, and a server Close frame with a standard code such as 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1013 ends the session instead of reconnecting (messages.rs:188-190; client.rs:348; messages.rs:62-64 with client.rs:142-157). It also sends audio before the vendor's connected frame and does not aggregate chunks to the 250 ms the vendor asks for (client.rs:90-97; mod.rs:100).

billing.notes: Billing is per stream, not per utterance: Rev AI charges the larger of stream duration and audio duration, rounded up to the second, with a 15 second minimum for each connection, so silence on an open stream is billed. Each connect also places a 10 minute credit hold, and another 5 minutes after every 5 minutes of stream time. Reconnects therefore add minimum charges. There is no Rev AI entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: Default for a Rev AI model id the map has never seen. Neither usual rule fits this vendor. File upload cannot be the default, because the only file interface is an asynchronous job answered in minutes. A plain 'every model streams' is not true either, because 'human' and the deprecated 'low_cost' and 'fusion' exist only on the job API. The row keeps today's behaviour, which is the choice that keeps the call working: the existing streaming client serves the session with the account's default streaming model, and the resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. The vendor audit recommends the stricter alternative, refusing unknown ids at setup; the capability-map workstream should decide between the two. No file-upload transport is listed on purpose. Rev AI's only file interface is the asynchronous job API (POST /jobs, then poll or webhook, then GET /jobs/{id}/transcript). The vendor describes its turnaround as '5 minutes or less' for short files, its tutorial says to wait 'approximately 1 minute', and each file is billed a 15 second minimum. The fact-check concluded that Rev AI must never be wrapped in the segmented adapter. Opening one short socket per utterance and sending EOS to force a final was also rejected: each connection bills 15 seconds, places a 10 minute credit hold and counts against the limit of 10 concurrent streams. The provider's native_model_handling (substituted) is what makes the resolver attach that warning.

gateway_client.notes: No code exists for this transport; two constants for it are declared and unused (mod.rs:54 and :60). The Reverie text-to-speech client already sends the same REV-API-KEY, REV-APP-ID and REV-APPNAME headers and is a pattern to copy. The request is multipart form data with the field audio_file, plus the headers src_lang (the language, required), domain (required) and format. The format value is a header, not a form field; 16k_int16 is the vendor's default and means 16 kHz signed 16-bit WAV. The response is one JSON object with text, display_text, a confidence between 0 and 1, success and cause. The adapter should treat success false, empty text or the cause 'audio too short' as a dropped segment, and should send logging false unless the customer opts in, because the vendor stores audio and transcripts when logging is on. The vendor's pages disagree on the request shape: the API reference and both official SDKs use POST / with the field audio_file, while two guide pages show POST /upload with the field file; the first is recorded. MP3 appears as a format value in one documentation example but is not in the format list, so it is not listed as accepted.

gateway_client.defect: The existing WebSocket client cannot hold a call with more than one utterance. One of two things happens, depending on a detail of the vendor's replies that was read from the documentation and not checked against the live service. If the replies carry the confidence value as a number, as the vendor documents, the client declares that field as text, cannot parse any reply, and produces no transcript at all. If the replies do parse, the client treats the first final result as the end of the session, because it never sets the vendor's continuous flag, and every later audio frame fails with 'Not connected'.
gateway_client.notes: This is the client every Reverie session gets today. The two defects described under defect exclude each other: if result frames fail to parse the client emits nothing at all, and if they parse the call gets one utterance. Either way a call with several turns does not work. Also found by reading: vendor error frames are not recognised as errors (messages.rs:153-169); the client sends timeout=15 and silence=1 and stores both as whole seconds (config.rs:297-302) although the vendor documents them as fractional numbers; and vendor-side storage of audio is on by default (config.rs:240-244). The repository's own mock test documents the one-utterance behaviour. The repair the audit proposes is to send continuous=1 and timeout=180, accept the confidence as a number or as text, and reconnect when the vendor closes with the cause 'timeout'. Once repaired and checked against the live service this transport should be marked as working and moved ahead of the file upload, because it is the only one that gives text while the caller is still speaking.

billing.notes: Describes the streaming transport, the one a session gets today; the file transport has its own block. The vendor prices both the file product and the streaming product per hour of audio (pay-as-you-go INR 24.99 per hour). The price was read from the vendor's pricing page with certificate checking turned off, because that site's certificate had expired, so it is lower trust. All call audio is sent on the socket, so silence is recorded as billed. The minimum billed duration and the rounding are not published. There is no Reverie entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

provenance.notes: Reverie's API has no model parameter: one recognition engine is selected by language and domain, and the product is selected by an appname value (stt_stream, stt_file or stt_batch). The wildcard is therefore the only Reverie row and the provider default. Because the provider's model string is marked sensitive, this row is the declared answer for every Reverie session, not a guess, so its confidence is 'documented'. The three appname values are not rows: the gateway reads the session's model field as the customer's Reverie app id (gateway/src/core/stt/reverie/config.rs:515-521), so a row keyed by an appname would never match a real session. File upload keeps first place from version 1, but no release builds it, so it is never chosen; the vendor's streaming product shares its language and domain lists with the file product (the vendor does not state coverage per product, and the two sources read list the same languages for both), so the order should be reversed once the client is repaired. The asynchronous stt_batch product (upload, then poll; the official SDK waits 5 s before its second poll) is not listed because it cannot serve a call. No segment profile is given: 16 kHz 16-bit WAV is the vendor's default format and no other default needs to change. The audit suggests an 8 s request timeout as a placeholder; that is the auditor's estimate. The language (src_lang) and the domain are required and there is no automatic language detection. Every Reverie session is handed to the existing WebSocket client, so the session starts and then either stops transcribing after the first utterance or never produces a transcript. The map keeps that client as the transport a session gets, marked known broken and reported in ready.stt, because the integration decisions report a broken native client instead of refusing it.

rates.note: Published under one 'WebSocket Streaming' heading; whether the legacy and realtime sockets share one pool is not stated. The vendor's limiter also reacts to the burst rate of new connections and rejects with close code 1003.

gateway_client.notes: For an unknown id the client URL-encodes the string into the connect URL without any check (config.rs:249-250, 315-346), so the vendor decides whether it is accepted. This client dials the socket Sarvam now labels legacy (wss://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text/ws, config.rs:23). It returns one final transcript per utterance and no interim text. Each caller chunk is base64-encoded and sent at once as a JSON text frame (provider.rs:218-241); Sarvam's server-side voice detector ends the utterance; the gateway never sends a flush (flush_signal is fixed to false, config.rs:163). Differences from the vendor documentation, found by reading and not re-probed: the client matches voice-activity events named START and END while the vendor reference names them START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech (provider.rs:429, 447-460); the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:150-157); confidence is invented as 0.95 because the vendor sends none (provider.rs:430); finals are dropped if a 256-slot channel is full (provider.rs:433-444, 549); only 11 language codes are accepted and an empty language becomes hi-IN (config.rs:41-53, 146-150, 324-330); the codec check accepts 'pcm', which is not a vendor value, and rejects mu-law and A-law before any dial (config.rs:156-160, 333); no model id is checked (config.rs:315-346). The standard factory matches only the exact provider id 'sarvam' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:457). No vendor quality signal reaches the gateway on this transport, so none is listed. Sarvam returns language_probability on this socket only when it detects the language itself; this client cannot ask for that (an empty language becomes hi-IN, config.rs:146-150, and 'unknown' fails the language check, config.rs:41-53, 325-330), has no field for it in its response type (provider.rs:120-135), and reports a confidence that is the constant 0.95 (provider.rs:430). Validation rejects any session sample rate other than 8000 or 16000 Hz (config.rs:317-322). The /v1/realtime cascade sets the speech-to-text rate to 24000 (gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:34, 342), so a voice-agent session on that route, and any session at 24 kHz or 48 kHz, fails at setup on this transport. For an 8 kHz session the client writes 8000 into every audio frame (provider.rs:544); the vendor reference lists 16000, 22050 and 24000 for that field and says 8 kHz is set only on the connection, while the vendor's guide says to set it in both places, so the outcome for a telephone leg is unknown. The vendor's best-practices page says this socket closes after 60 seconds of inactivity and recommends silent audio as keep-alive. The client instead sends a JSON ping after 30 seconds without audio (config.rs:32; provider.rs:291-312), which is not a client message the vendor documents for this socket, and it treats any vendor error frame as fatal with no reconnect (provider.rs:254-260).
gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, not re-probed: voice-activity events are matched as START and END while the vendor sends START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech, and the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:429, 447-460, 150-157). Validation accepts only 8 kHz and 16 kHz linear PCM and 11 languages, so a 24 kHz /v1/realtime voice agent or a mu-law telephone leg fails at setup (config.rs:317-322, 324-333).

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text, multipart/form-data, file part named 'file', header api-subscription-key (an invalid key returns 403, not 401). Audio longer than 30 seconds returns 422, so the 25 second default segment plus padding must be checked against that cap before upload. The limit recorded, 60 requests per minute, is the Starter tier (Pro 100, Business 4,000); it is shared by every call on the Sarvam account across all keys, so a limiter above the per-session cap of two uploads is required. Retry only on 429, 500 and 503. The response has no transcript confidence, no no-speech probability and no word timestamps; an empty transcript is the only no-speech signal, and language_probability is present only when the language was auto-detected. WAV is detected automatically and is the vendor's recommended format; raw PCM needs input_audio_codec and must be 16 kHz. The vendor also accepts AMR and WMA, which the map's format list cannot name. Sarvam's batch job API (POST /speech-to-text/job/v1, then upload, start, poll, download) is answered in minutes and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

gateway_client.notes: The client has a mock end-to-end test and was verified live against this socket on 2026-06-04, but with the model saarika:v2.5, never with saaras:v3, so this row is recorded as wire-tested only. This client dials the socket Sarvam now labels legacy (wss://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text/ws, config.rs:23). It returns one final transcript per utterance and no interim text. Each caller chunk is base64-encoded and sent at once as a JSON text frame (provider.rs:218-241); Sarvam's server-side voice detector ends the utterance; the gateway never sends a flush (flush_signal is fixed to false, config.rs:163). Differences from the vendor documentation, found by reading and not re-probed: the client matches voice-activity events named START and END while the vendor reference names them START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech (provider.rs:429, 447-460); the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:150-157); confidence is invented as 0.95 because the vendor sends none (provider.rs:430); finals are dropped if a 256-slot channel is full (provider.rs:433-444, 549); only 11 language codes are accepted and an empty language becomes hi-IN (config.rs:41-53, 146-150, 324-330); the codec check accepts 'pcm', which is not a vendor value, and rejects mu-law and A-law before any dial (config.rs:156-160, 333); no model id is checked (config.rs:315-346). The standard factory matches only the exact provider id 'sarvam' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:457). No vendor quality signal reaches the gateway on this transport, so none is listed. Sarvam returns language_probability on this socket only when it detects the language itself; this client cannot ask for that (an empty language becomes hi-IN, config.rs:146-150, and 'unknown' fails the language check, config.rs:41-53, 325-330), has no field for it in its response type (provider.rs:120-135), and reports a confidence that is the constant 0.95 (provider.rs:430). Validation rejects any session sample rate other than 8000 or 16000 Hz (config.rs:317-322). The /v1/realtime cascade sets the speech-to-text rate to 24000 (gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:34, 342), so a voice-agent session on that route, and any session at 24 kHz or 48 kHz, fails at setup on this transport. For an 8 kHz session the client writes 8000 into every audio frame (provider.rs:544); the vendor reference lists 16000, 22050 and 24000 for that field and says 8 kHz is set only on the connection, while the vendor's guide says to set it in both places, so the outcome for a telephone leg is unknown. The vendor's best-practices page says this socket closes after 60 seconds of inactivity and recommends silent audio as keep-alive. The client instead sends a JSON ping after 30 seconds without audio (config.rs:32; provider.rs:291-312), which is not a client message the vendor documents for this socket, and it treats any vendor error frame as fatal with no reconnect (provider.rs:254-260).
gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, not re-probed: voice-activity events are matched as START and END while the vendor sends START_SPEECH and END_SPEECH, so every final is flagged end of speech, and the error frame is parsed for data.message while the vendor sends data.error (provider.rs:429, 447-460, 150-157). Validation accepts only 8 kHz and 16 kHz linear PCM and 11 languages, so a 24 kHz /v1/realtime voice agent or a mu-law telephone leg fails at setup (config.rs:317-322, 324-333).

gateway_client.notes: Synchronous request: POST https://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text, multipart/form-data, file part named 'file', header api-subscription-key (an invalid key returns 403, not 401). Audio longer than 30 seconds returns 422, so the 25 second default segment plus padding must be checked against that cap before upload. The limit recorded, 60 requests per minute, is the Starter tier (Pro 100, Business 4,000); it is shared by every call on the Sarvam account across all keys, so a limiter above the per-session cap of two uploads is required. Retry only on 429, 500 and 503. The response has no transcript confidence, no no-speech probability and no word timestamps; an empty transcript is the only no-speech signal, and language_probability is present only when the language was auto-detected. WAV is detected automatically and is the vendor's recommended format; raw PCM needs input_audio_codec and must be 16 kHz. The vendor also accepts AMR and WMA, which the map's format list cannot name. Sarvam's batch job API (POST /speech-to-text/job/v1, then upload, start, poll, download) is answered in minutes and is not a live transport, so it is not listed.

billing.notes: Each upload is billed per second of uploaded audio, rounded up, with a 1 second minimum (vendor FAQ); only uploaded segments are billed. No pricing_key exists for Sarvam speech-to-text.

Priced per hour of audio and billed per second, rounded up to the next second, with a 1 second minimum charge (vendor FAQ). The FAQ does not say whether the minimum applies per REST request or per socket session. Whether silence on an open socket is billed is not stated. There is no Sarvam speech-to-text entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

gateway_client.notes: This is the gateway-driven commit on a vendor socket. The realtime socket sends partial transcripts while the caller speaks and offers endpointing=manual, where the client sends speech_start, speech_end and flush; with endpointing=vad the vendor's own detector ends the utterance instead, which is why the owner is 'either'. With manual endpointing the gateway's detector decides the boundary and no upload round trip is needed, so the audit rates this the better investment for real-time quality than file upload. Wire differences from the legacy socket that the new client must handle: audio is sent as {"event":"audio_input","audio":"<base64>"}; raw PCM only (linear16, linear32, mulaw, alaw at 8 or 16 kHz); auto-detect is 'auto' and Odia is 'or-IN' (the legacy socket and REST use 'unknown' and 'od-IN'); language_code is required; keep-alive is ping and pong; session.end reports the billed audio duration. The final transcript carries no confidence and no word list; language_confidence is the only quality signal. Pipecat's 1.00 s constant for this socket is marked provisional and is not a measurement, so the latency is recorded as unmeasured.

gateway_client.notes: The request, token and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /rest/v1/speech:recognize, raw audio body) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: send headerless PCM16 with Content-Type audio/x-pcm;bit=16;rate=<rate> and the sample_rate query parameter (Sber has no audio/wav type; PCM with a WAV header under the same type is also documented as accepted); keep uploads under 60 s and 2 MB (the client's own cap is 2 MiB and its 60 s constant is never enforced, config.rs:35-38); send the acoustic model as the 'model' query parameter (today it comes only from extras["model"], config.rs:351-356); share one OAuth token cache and one HTTP client across sessions; map HTTP 429 to back-off and 404 to 'unknown model'; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 0.95 (client.rs:439-443). The synchronous response carries text, emotions and speaker age and gender only: no confidence, no word times, no detected language. Hints are not available on this endpoint. The vendor recognises only the first channel of multichannel audio on this endpoint, so the adapter must send mono. The gateway's feature matrix nevertheless lists 'multichannel' for this provider and the client can send channels_count (gateway/src/core/capabilities.rs:346, config.rs:394-396), a claim this endpoint cannot honour (inferred from the vendor text, not run). The token's expiry field (expires_at) must be accepted in either seconds or milliseconds: the vendor's pages disagree, and the legacy client assumes milliseconds (gateway/src/core/stt/sberdevices/messages.rs:16-30), so if the API returns seconds every upload would first fetch a new token.

segment_profile.rationale: The vendor limits parallel recognition streams per account: its API documentation says 10 for legal entities and 5 for individuals, while its FAQ says 50 and 1. Both documentation figures are recorded in limits.rates by plan (legal_entity 10, individual 5), and the individual figure is assumed when the deployment names no plan: it is below both figures for legal entities and above the FAQ's single stream for individuals. The limiter should be set per credential, and the OAuth scope the session already carries says which kind of account it is (SALUTE_SPEECH_PERS for individuals, SALUTE_SPEECH_CORP and SALUTE_SPEECH_B2B for legal entities). Two uploads in flight per call would let a handful of calls exhaust the account, so one per call plus an account-wide limiter. The 10000 ms request timeout, with about 3 s to connect, is the vendor audit's engineering judgement, not a measurement: no latency is published, and the legacy client's 60 s request and 30 s connect timeouts (gateway/src/core/stt/sberdevices/config.rs:311-312) would stall a turn. Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin.

gateway_client.notes: The request, token and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /rest/v1/speech:recognize, raw audio body) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. provenance.notes: Provider default for any model id on an OpenAI-compatible self-hosted deployment. It fails slow: a wrong file-upload guess costs about one to two seconds a turn, a wrong streaming guess costs the call. The file-transcription route is the one interface nearly every such server has; realtime sockets are not standardised (at least five different message sets answer on the path /v1/realtime), and a socket that accepts audio often hides a batch model. Nothing a server reports about itself says whether a model streams, so a deployment moves off this row only by an operator declaration that selects a named profile. Per-server request restrictions, which is why the request is kept to file, model, response_format=json and a language the transcriber may drop: WaaV Infer answers HTTP 400 to a non-empty language or prompt, to verbose_json (it accepts only json and text) and to a non-zero temperature, and requires the model field to be empty or to name the loaded family. vLLM caps uploads at 25 MB by default, silently chunks audio longer than 30 s, and its verbose_json has no no_speech_prob. The whisper.cpp server runs one inference at a time, takes WAV only unless started with --convert, and serves /inference unless remapped. NVIDIA Speech NIM takes WAV, OPUS or FLAC only, offers json or text only, and requires a BCP-47 language or a model. speaches runs its own voice detector over every upload and may download a model on first use. LocalAI defaults to json. A 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV is the only upload every one of them accepts. Because no server is guaranteed to return a no-speech probability or a log probability, dropping bad transcripts must rest on the gateway's own voice detector and on text filters.

provenance.notes: Family rule for any model id containing 'whisper', for example openai/whisper-large-v3 (the id in the gateway's own deployment fixture), Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3 or whisper-1. Whisper is file-only on every server checked: on vLLM only the Voxtral Realtime and Qwen3-ASR realtime model classes support the realtime task, so the socket route is not even registered for Whisper; NVIDIA states 'The Whisper model supports offline mode only'; the whisper.cpp server has no socket; sherpa-onnx serves Whisper only from its non-streaming server; WaaV Infer serves it one whole clip at a time. Whisper attends to 30 seconds at once: vLLM chunks longer audio on the server and WaaV Infer cuts it at hard 30 second boundaries, so the gateway's 25 second segment cap must not be raised. Servers that put a socket in front of Whisper (speaches, LocalAI with server voice detection, WhisperLiveKit) run the batch model per utterance or re-decode a growing window behind it; those are reachable only through a deployment override that selects a profile. gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock server. Finals are word groups released on the vendor's max_delay timer, which the client always sets to 2 seconds (mod.rs:59, client.rs:420). They are marked final but not speech-final, so the gateway's transcript timers end the turn, unless the session sets utterance_end_ms, which turns on the vendor's silence trigger (config.rs:753-755, client.rs:468-470). The client sends the deprecated operating_point field, never model, always dials the EU host (config.rs:652), and accepts the language value 'auto', which the vendor documents as batch only. The 50 concurrent sessions limit is the Pro plan figure (2 on the Free plan).

gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/batch.rs:839-844 and gateway/src/core/stt/prerecorded.rs:117-124 (no Speechmatics file builder exists)
gateway_client.notes: Needs a multipart request with a 'config' part (JSON using model, not operating_point) and a 'data_file' part, bearer authentication, a per-region https base URL (the existing endpoint override accepts only ws and wss), handling of the job states created, done, rejected and deleted, and a best-effort delete of the job afterwards. The blocking wait parameter exists only on the hosted service; a self-hosted batch container needs submit and poll.

segment_profile.rationale: The request is POST /v2/jobs/?wait=10&format=json-v2, which blocks until the job finishes or the wait elapses, so each HTTP call gets 12 seconds, slightly longer than the wait. If the job is still running the adapter makes one GET of the transcript with a wait, then fails the segment. The server caps the wait at an unpublished value. The adapter should delete each job after reading it, because the batch service keeps audio for 7 days. All other defaults hold: the vendor names 16-bit 16 kHz mono WAV as the fastest format for very short files and bills to the second.

measurements.conditions: A 30-minute file usually completes within 10 seconds ('通常30分钟音频可在10秒内完成识别'). A throughput figure for long files, not a latency for segments of 2 to 25 seconds; it does not seed the deadline.

latency.notes: The vendor publishes only a throughput figure for flash (30 minutes of audio usually within 10 seconds).

rates.note: Free concurrency per account (AppId) for standard engines, shared by every call on the account; add-on packs buy more.

context_params.note: Entries are written 'word|weight' and joined with commas; a word is at most 30 characters.

gateway_client.notes: Raw audio body. The signature is the socket's HMAC-SHA1 scheme (signature.rs:502-534) with 'POST' prefixed to the string to sign, sent in an Authorization header; the timestamp must be within 3 minutes of server time. A non-zero 'code' in an HTTP 200 reply is an error; 4006 is account concurrency exceeded and should be treated as back-pressure.

segment_profile.rationale: 6000 ms is the audit's starting value, not a measurement; no short-clip latency is published. Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin.

rates.note: Default concurrent connections per account on the China site, the only site that lists this engine.

context_params.note: Entries are written 'word|weight' and joined with commas; a word is at most 30 characters.

gateway_client.defect: Known broken against the vendor protocol: in-progress partial results (slice_type 1) are marked final, the vendor end message is never sent, and a void voice_id is reused on reconnect. gateway_client.notes: The defect list with line references is in the provider notes. This id is not in the client's engine list (config.rs:129-149); from_str lower-cases its input and falls back to 16k_zh (config.rs:153, :173).

rates.note: Default request rate per account; QPS packs buy more.

gateway_client.notes: JSON body with Base64 audio in 'Data', signed with TC3-HMAC-SHA256. The only such signer is private to the Tencent text-to-speech provider (provider.rs:141-206) with the service name fixed to 'tts' (:148). The 3 MB limit is measured after Base64; 60 seconds of 16 kHz PCM16 is 1.92 MB raw, so the 60 second limit binds first. The vendor's default rate limit is 30 requests per second per account; limits.rates keeps that per-second window.

segment_profile.rationale: 6000 ms is the audit's starting value, not a measurement. Uploads stay per pause although billing is per call: at about 15 uploads a minute a call-hour costs about what an hour of flash audio costs at top-tier prices, so holding a whole turn to save calls is not worth the delay. The audit suggested merging a turn's segments; an operator who prefers that can set upload_policy per_turn.

billing.notes: SentenceRecognition: per call whatever the length.
Flash: per second of uploaded audio, under one second billed as one second.

gateway_client.defect: The existing streaming client does not match the vendor protocol. Found by reading the client against the vendor proto and by inspecting the certificate chain; nothing was run against the vendor. (1) api.tinkoff.ai chains to the Russian Trusted Root CA; the gRPC channel is given no extra root (gateway/src/core/stt/tinkoff/grpc.rs:49) and a stock operating-system trust store does not contain it. (2) The client sends x-api-key and x-secret-key metadata where the vendor requires 'authorization: Bearer <JWT>' (grpc.rs:70-86). (3) It reads results from protobuf field 1 where the vendor uses field 2, so every response decodes as empty and is dropped (messages.rs:491-496, provider.rs:146-149). (4) It decodes each result without the vendor's recognition_result nesting (messages.rs:583-588).
gateway_client.notes: Bidirectional gRPC StreamingRecognize at api.tinkoff.ai:443; audio is forwarded unbuffered and the vendor's voice-activity detector ends phrases (silence threshold 0.6 s by default); is_final is copied to is_speech_final (provider.rs:419-426). Further defects: every audio-encoding number except LINEAR16 is wrong (config.rs:381-390), and num_channels is not sent for mono although the vendor marks it mandatory (messages.rs:364-368). The mock end-to-end test encodes the gateway's own schema (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1705-1707), so it cannot detect any of this. The vendor guarantees connection continuity only under 3 min 25 s (hard cap one hour), so reconnects are normal within a call. The vendor returns a 'relative confidence factor' per alternative and a per-word confidence that may be negative; neither is a 0 to 1 probability, so quality_signals is empty and the value must not be thresholded. Speech-context phrases map to the gateway's keyterms feature.

billing.notes: Billed per second of audio, with three tariffs: stream, online file (lower than stream) and deferred. No per-request minimum is published. No pricing key exists for this provider in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs. This block describes the stream, the only transport usable with today's code. bills_silence is null because the vendor does not say whether the stream tariff counts silence: it is charged per second of audio and the gateway forwards all call audio, so silence is very probably billed.

gateway_client.notes: Current vendor interface (documented and probed): POST https://viettelai.vn/asr/recognize, multipart fields file and token; reply {code, message, response.result[]} with transcript, confidence, word_alignment[] (word, beg, end, confidence) and segment; errors use {code, en_message, vi_message}; an invalid token returns HTTP 404. The existing client (ViettelStt::process_audio) does not match it: it posts to https://viettelgroup.ai/voice/api/asr/v1/rest/decode_file (config.rs:40), a domain re-registered by a third party on 2025-11-14 that does not resolve today; it sends the token as a header, which the current endpoint ignores (client.rs:157); and its parser expects {status, result} (config.rs:183-211), so a real success reads as an empty transcript and is dropped (inferred from reading, not run). It also hard-codes confidence 0.96 (client.rs:267), has no circuit breaker, never invokes its error callback and forwards any model string as an asr_model header the vendor does not define (client.rs:166-168). Its only test checks the gateway's assumed reply against the gateway's own mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:1031-1054). On non-speech audio the vendor returned an invented word with confidence 0.007, so a confidence floor is the natural filter here.

segment_profile.rationale: Provisional. Every anonymous probe that carried audio took longer than a normal conversational budget (15.7 s and 22.5 s for 3 s of audio) and the vendor cites about 30 seconds per file, so a shorter timeout would fail every request. Replace it with the measured P99 plus a margin once a paid token is available; if that number is not within the segment deadline, do not enable this transport. All other settings stay at the gateway defaults: the vendor documents no limit, no minimum billing and no concurrency figure for speech-to-text.

transports.disabled_reason: The gateway has no streaming client for this vendor (not implemented). The vendor documents a live WebSocket interface, which is the right primary path for calls; once a client is built and its message format is confirmed with a valid token, this transport should be moved ahead of the file upload.

gateway_client.notes: The provider directory holds only an HTTP client (client.rs, config.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs). Vendor interface as documented: wss://viettelai.vn/websocket/asr/ws/decode_online, with the audio format (raw PCM16, rate and channels) and the token in the query string; binary audio frames about four times a second; the text 'EOS' ends recognition, or the server ends it shortly after the last voice (hence endpointing_owner 'either'). Probed without credentials: the upgrade returns 101 with any token, the server stays silent until audio arrives, then sends the text 'Invalid token' and drops the socket with no close frame, so connect() cannot validate credentials. Unconfirmed until a probe with a valid token: whether interim hypotheses and a final flag are sent (the protocol resembles the open-source kaldi-gstreamer-server, which sends both; recorded here as 'none'), the frame size (the vendor's prose and its sample code disagree), which sample rates are accepted (the documented URL carries 48000; 16000 is a worked example), and whether status 9 means 'no data' or 'all recognisers busy'.

billing.notes: A socket is sent all call audio, and the vendor bills seconds of audio from the same prepaid packages.

rates.note: Synchronous recognition requests. Whether the quota is per folder or per cloud is not stated.

gateway_client.notes: The request and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /speech/v1/stt:recognize) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: send headerless PCM16, not WAV (the vendor accepts only LPCM without a WAV header, or OggOpus); send sampleRateHertz equal to the upload rate as well as format=lpcm (the vendor default is 48000 and only 8000, 16000 and 48000 are accepted); keep every upload under 30 s and 1 MB including pre-roll and trailing silence (the legacy overflow cap of 1,024,000 bytes at client.rs:37 is 32 s at 16 kHz); never upload a segment without speech, because an empty request is billed one 15 s unit; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 0.95 (client.rs:293-297). limits.rates records the vendor quota of 20 synchronous requests per second in the vendor's own window; the limiter must hold the per-second rate. An HTTP 429 currently counts as a failure on the breaker shared by every Yandex session (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:137-140).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 8000 ms in total, with about 2 s to connect, is the vendor audit's provisional value, not a measurement: Yandex publishes no latency for the synchronous endpoint, and the legacy client allows 60 s with no connect timeout (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:22-26). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit the vendor limits: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB at 16 kHz, inside 30 s and 1 MB; the adapter should still refuse to send more than 29 s, and must never upload 48 kHz PCM, where 1 MB holds about 10.9 s. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause).

refusal.text: Asynchronous job only. The vendor accepts this tag only on AsyncRecognizer.RecognizeFile (submit, then poll), says asynchronous recognition takes from several minutes up to 24 hours, and caps it at 500 requests per hour. There is no streaming interface and no synchronous file endpoint for it. For a live call choose general.

billing.notes: Asynchronous recognition is billed one 15 s unit and then per second from the 16th second. Recorded for completeness; the model has no live path.

transports.disabled_reason: The per-utterance file-upload adapter (segmented_yandex) is not implemented. The Yandex client registered today is not a substitute: it uploads whatever audio accumulated about every 500 ms on a wall-clock timer, speech or silence, and marks each piece as the end of a turn (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:219-332). Enable once the adapter ships and one live call has passed.

rates.note: Synchronous recognition requests. Whether the quota is per folder or per cloud is not stated.

gateway_client.notes: The request and response code for the synchronous endpoint (POST /speech/v1/stt:recognize) already exists inside the legacy client and can be lifted into the adapter. The adapter must: send headerless PCM16, not WAV (the vendor accepts only LPCM without a WAV header, or OggOpus); send sampleRateHertz equal to the upload rate as well as format=lpcm (the vendor default is 48000 and only 8000, 16000 and 48000 are accepted); keep every upload under 30 s and 1 MB including pre-roll and trailing silence (the legacy overflow cap of 1,024,000 bytes at client.rs:37 is 32 s at 16 kHz); never upload a segment without speech, because an empty request is billed one 15 s unit; and report confidence as unknown instead of the hard-coded 0.95 (client.rs:293-297). limits.rates records the vendor quota of 20 synchronous requests per second in the vendor's own window; the limiter must hold the per-second rate. An HTTP 429 currently counts as a failure on the breaker shared by every Yandex session (gateway/src/core/stt/http_resilience.rs:137-140).

segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. 8000 ms in total, with about 2 s to connect, is the vendor audit's provisional value, not a measurement: Yandex publishes no latency for the synchronous endpoint, and the legacy client allows 60 s with no connect timeout (gateway/src/core/stt/yandex/client.rs:22-26). Replace it with measured P99 plus a margin. The other defaults fit the vendor limits: a 25 s segment with 400 ms pre-roll and 500 ms trailing silence is 25.9 s and about 829 kB at 16 kHz, inside 30 s and 1 MB; the adapter should still refuse to send more than 29 s, and must never upload 48 kHz PCM, where 1 MB holds about 10.9 s. Because every request is billed in 15 s units (billing.increment_ms), segments of the same turn that are still queued should be merged while the merged upload stays within 15 s. An upload must never be held back to wait for a merge, so upload_policy stays at the default (upload at each pause).

gateway_client.notes: Vendor endpointing through the default end-of-utterance classifier (sensitivity DEFAULT or HIGH, with a pause hint). provenance.notes: Meaning: take today's path unchanged (passthrough). The resolver calls create_stt_standard(provider, config) exactly as the voice manager does today (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:197-205) and changes nothing else: it does not install the segmenter, does not apply a dialect and uploads nothing. A provider registered at run time or through the plugin interface gets its own factory, as today. A name nobody registered gets today's setup error, "Unknown STT provider" (create_stt_standard at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:390-478, whose fallback arm at :476 calls create_stt_provider, gateway/src/core/stt/mod.rs:488-495, which asks the registry, gateway/src/plugin/registry.rs:303-340). Why not file upload. An OpenAI-compatible server never reaches this row: it arrives as vendor self_hosted (or one of its three aliases) and has its own default row. What does reach it is a provider with its own factory and its own wire protocol. Uploading that provider's audio as an OpenAI multipart request has no address to go to, because the speech-to-text configuration carries no base address (gateway/src/core/stt/base.rs:503-519). The nearest existing fallback is the OpenAI client's production host (gateway/src/core/stt/openai/config.rs:29-49), and using it would send another vendor's API key to a third party. A file-upload default would also silently reroute every runtime-registered plugin that streams correctly today. Why not a refusal. An empty transport list with a refusal would refuse providers that work today; the gateway's rule for uncatalogued providers is that unknown does not mean unsupported (gateway/src/core/capabilities.rs:674-682). What the customer sees. A name nobody registered still fails at session setup with today's error. A provider that was registered works as today, and the session-start announcement should say that the capability was assumed from the global default and report interim results and endpointing as unknown. A counter keyed by provider shows which unknown names are in use, which is the queue for new rows. Known residual risk. A runtime-registered client that buffers audio until the call ends will go on doing so. Proposed additive safeguard: after the client is built, read BaseSTT::is_request_response() (gateway/src/core/stt/base.rs:805); when it is true the client answers only when the call ends, so emit a coded warning and count it, without rerouting.
